name: Life Globe
blurb: ARPG resource orb: sloshing liquid with a lit meniscus, swirling body, glass lens highlights and a forged rim.
port: UMG or UI Toolkit: one material on an image widget with Fill as a scalar parameter driven by gameplay. Keep it in a single pass so it batches with the HUD.
notes: The sphere is faked in 2D: a disc SDF gives a normal, which bends the liquid lookup so the surface appears to wrap.
The fill line is two sine waves plus noise; the meniscus is a thin bright band along that line with foam above it.
Body colour is noise swirled in polar space and darkened toward the bottom to suggest thickness.
Low health switches on a slow red pulse and faster slosh: UI effects should communicate state, not decorate.

name: Earth Spikes
blurb: A fissure races along the ground and a line of rock spikes punches up behind it, each one larger than the last, then the row crumbles back into the floor.
port: Niagara: a mesh emitter spawning along a spline with spawn delay by index and a scale curve with overshoot. Material is a standard lit rock with an emissive crack mask on Dynamic Parameter. The fissure is a decal with a panning reveal mask.
notes: A glowing fissure runs ahead of the spikes by a quarter second. That is the anticipation beat and it tells the player where the damage will land.
All spikes are one draw: a plane rolled into six-sided cones in the vertex shader with hashed radius per vertex so every spike has a chiselled silhouette.
Each spike is thrust up from below the floor with an overshoot curve, 75 ms after its neighbour. Height ramps along the line so the row builds to a peak.
Rock is lit and opaque with facet normals. The crack channel of the noise sheet glows near the base and cools, which ties the mesh to the tint.
Dust, chips and sparks are timed per spike inside the particle sim, so one emitter of each kind serves the whole row.

name: Bone Spear
blurb: A spectral bone lance knits itself together, launches through the target and shatters at the end of its range, leaving a ghostly wake.
port: Niagara: a mesh projectile with a masked dissolve material, two ribbon emitters with a spiral offset, and burst emitters fired by collision events. The wake can be a ribbon with a material erosion driven by ribbon age.
notes: Anticipation is half a second: motes converge, the spear resolves through a noise alpha clip with a hot edge, and it draws back before release.
The wake is stored in world space. Every point on the path knows when the spear passed it, so age since passing drives the erosion and the widening with no history buffer.
Two spiral ribbons use the same pass time to open out behind the spear like a rifled vortex wake.
Shock collars stand perpendicular to the flight line at the muzzle, the pierce point and two mid-air points. They are four quads packed into one mesh.
Bone shards are alpha blended and lit, not additive, so they stay readable as solid debris against the glow.

name: Inner Flame
src: Fills an enemy with fire that leaks when hit and explodes when it dies.
blurb: A hex that turns a body into a furnace: light climbs through the seams of the armour, blows out in jets when it is struck, and ends in a detonation that leaves burning ground.
port: Character material with a fill scalar for the seams, then swap to a fractured mesh or Niagara mesh debris on death. The leak jets are socketed burst emitters triggered from hit events. Fire clouds are looping emitters with a scale-down curve.
notes: The build-up lives in the victim material. Crack noise thresholded by a fill value opens glowing seams outward from the chest, with a pulse that speeds up as the fill rises.
Two hits land before the end. Each one jolts the body and vents a jet of flame from the chest seam, which is the leak the spell description promises.
On death the body is alpha-clipped away in one frame and replaced by 84 instanced armour fragments on ballistic arcs with one bounce. Their inner faces stay hot and cool over a second.
Flame clouds remain: four ground fires burn down over two seconds on a scorch decal whose cracks cool last.

name: Fireball
src: Hurls a ball of fire that explodes on impact, burning everything in a small radius.
blurb: A roiling ball of fire leaves the hand on a flat line, detonates on the target and collapses into soot, embers and a cooling scorch.
port: Niagara: projectile emitter with a collision event that fires burst emitters. Fire and soot share one material with a temperature Dynamic Parameter feeding a blackbody curve; the char is a decal plus a per-instance scalar on the character material.
notes: The explosion is alpha blended, not additive. Each puff carries a hot core that cools into lit soot, so the fireball has dark creases and real volume.
The projectile is a displaced sphere with a sooty flame trail. A point light rides it across the floor and spikes on the hit.
The impact frame is a hard spiked burst held for about three frames, then the lighting carries the scale.
Residue: a scorch decal with cooling cracks, charred armour on the target and small flames that keep licking the body.

name: Flame Tongue
src: Launched a short-ranged tongue of flame at a nearby target. Removed in 0.25.
blurb: A living ribbon of fire whips out from the hand, licks up the breastplate with a curled tip and recoils into soot.
port: Niagara ribbon emitter along a spline component whose control points are animated by curves, with a second emitter sampling the same spline for soot puffs and drips. The singe is a character material layer keyed to the contact time.
notes: The tongue is a camera-facing ribbon built on an animated cubic bezier, so it lashes and curls instead of flying straight like a bolt.
Width is profiled like a real tongue: narrow root, fat belly and a pointed tip that curls upward where it touches.
Small licks are spawned along the same path and rise off the ribbon, and a ghost of lit smoke hangs on the curve after it recoils.
Burning droplets fall off the ribbon and leave cooling specks on the stone. The target keeps a singe mark with a dying ember rim.

name: Hellfire Mortar
src: Splits the ground into a lava-filled chasm along which a mortar travels, firing magma at enemies.
blurb: The floor unzips into a glowing trench, a basalt mortar surfaces in the lava and grinds along it, lobbing shells of magma that splash and cool where they land.
port: The trench is a decal with a parallax occlusion or bump offset node and a flow-mapped lava material. The mortar is a small rigged mesh moved along a spline. Shells and splatter are Niagara mesh particles with collision, plus a cooling curve on emissive.
notes: The chasm is a parallax decal: the lava surface is sampled a fixed depth below the floor along the view ray, so the far wall shows and the trench reads as a real cut.
Broken slabs along both lips are instanced lit rocks that hop as the crack passes, then sit in the glow of the lava.
The mortar is a lathed basalt barrel on a rock base. It rises out of the flow, tracks each foe, recoils when it fires and keeps a hot muzzle.
Shells are crusted magma meshes on a true ballistic arc. Each impact throws viscous blobs that land, flatten and cool from yellow to dull red.

name: Fire Storm
src: Calls down a massive storm of flame on a target area, leaving behind fire vortices.
blurb: Fire rains into a ring, a column slams down and a raymarched dome of flame swallows the area, then three fire vortices prowl the scorched ground.
port: Hero version: a baked VDB or a heterogeneous volume for the dome, with Niagara for rain, pillars and debris. Vortices are a twisted cylinder mesh with a panning spiral material and a vortex force on the sprite emitter.
notes: The explosion is a real volume: a raymarched dome and descending column cut from 3D noise, with a temperature field that maps to flame colour and soot that absorbs light.
The tell is falling streaks of fire and a floor that starts to glow in blotches. The strike frame is the white-hot core of the volume plus a hard shock ring on the stone.
Paving is blasted outward as instanced lit rock that bounces and stays, and tall pillars of flame punch up through the dome for the first second.
The spell leaves three vortices: twisted tube meshes with spiral noise, wrapped in orbiting flame sprites, each with its own light, wandering until they starve.

name: Ring of Flames
src: Surrounded the caster with a moving ring of fire clouds and granted fire resistance. Removed in 0.26.
blurb: Eight clouds of fire circle the caster as one leaning wall of flame, scorching a ring into the floor while the ground inside the ward stays clean.
port: A ring mesh with a volumetric fire material for gameplay distance, or this raymarch in a bounding cylinder for close shots. Attach to the character root. Smoke and sparks are Niagara emitters on a ring location with an orbit velocity.
notes: The wall is one raymarched torus of volume noise. Its height is modulated eight times around the circle, one swell per adjacent tile, and the swells orbit.
Flames lean back against the direction of travel, so the ring reads as moving even in a still.
The caster is lit from every side by three orbiting lights. A thin ward circle and an unburnt disc of floor say the wearer is protected.
It is an ambient loop driven by time only, with smoke shearing off the top, sparks spiralling up and a charred annulus under the fire.

name: Hailstorm
src: Batters creatures in a ring around the caster with hail, sparing adjacent ones.
blurb: A dark shelf of vapour gathers overhead and drops a ring of hailstones that hammer the floor around the caster, bounce and stay.
port: Niagara: mesh renderer for the stones with a collision module and one bounce, a ribbon or stretched sprite emitter for the streaks, and collision events that spawn chips and six-way lit puffs. The frost annulus is a decal with a threshold driven by elapsed time.
notes: The safe zone is drawn first: one hard ring snaps out from the caster and is gone in three frames, so the clear centre reads before any hail lands.
Hailstones are instanced rock meshes with the shared ice material. Each has a closed-form fall, one hop on landing, then rests on the floor as residue.
Every stone is led by a thin lit streak and followed by two chips and a frost puff that share its landing hash, so impacts line up without any collision pass.
Two cold point lights jump around the ring every few frames, which makes the barrage flicker on the armour and columns without any large glow sprite.

name: Summon Ice Beast
src: Summons an ice beast ally.
blurb: Frost spirals in across the floor and freezes upward, crystal by crystal, into a hulking four-legged beast that lifts its head and breathes.
port: For a shipping creature this is a skeletal mesh with a dissolve material. The assembling look ports as a Niagara mesh emitter that samples skeleton sockets, with per-instance scale curves and a shared ice material.
notes: The beast is 52 instanced crystal meshes. A small table in the vertex shader places legs, torso, hump, head, jaw, horns and tail, and the rest are hashed spines.
Growth runs from the ground up: feet first, then the body, then the head and spines. Each crystal overshoots slightly as it locks in.
The wake beat is the impact frame: eyes ignite, the head rears, a hard spiked flash sits behind the skull for three frames and vapour is blown across the floor.
Rime is weighted to upward facets so the top planes read white and the flanks stay dark, clear and reflective.

name: Frozen Ramparts
src: Coats nearby walls in ice that damages and slows foes next to them until the caster moves.
blurb: Ice races out along the dungeon walls from the caster, sheathing the masonry, throwing spikes at anyone standing close and pouring cold vapour onto the floor.
port: Unreal: a world-space sphere mask in the wall material driven by a material parameter collection, with spikes as a Niagara mesh emitter sampling the wall surface. The rime on characters is an overlay material with a directional mask.
notes: The walls are two lit masonry boxes. One distance field from the caster drives everything: the ice sheath, the spike growth, the vapour and the floor frost all read the same front.
The sheath is a material swap with a white rime band on the leading edge, so the front reads as freezing rather than as a wipe.
Spikes and icicles are instanced crystals that pop out as the front passes. The largest ones are aimed at the two foes by the wall.
Foes beside the wall collect a rime shell on the wall side and are lit by small cold flashes each time the ramparts bite.

name: Metabolic Englaciation
src: Slows all non-cold-resistant creatures near the caster.
blurb: A low wall of cold rolls out from the caster. As it crosses each creature their body heat is torn off as dying embers and they stiffen under a skin of rime.
port: Niagara: a ring emitter with radius on a curve for the fog front, a decal with a radial threshold for the frost, and a character overlay material with a per-actor freeze scalar set from the same curve. Animation slowdown is a play rate change on hit.
notes: The hex is told through contrast. Before the wave each foe sheds faint amber heat and sways freely. After it they are lit blue, glazed with ice and nearly still.
The slowdown is real: the actor sway is driven by a phase that stops integrating when the front arrives, and the rime shell follows the same pose in the vertex shader.
The front is a rolling bank of lit vapour with one hard line on the floor and a refraction ripple, not a glowing dome.
A thin crescent is held for three frames on each body where the front hits it.

name: Splinterfrost Shell
src: Builds a half-circle barricade of ice in front of the caster that fires icy shards when segments are destroyed.
blurb: Iron stakes punch out of the floor, ice slabs grow between them into a banded barricade, and the segment an attacker breaks answers with a volley of shards.
port: Niagara mesh renderers for slabs, shards and chunks with a collision module for the embedded shards. The slab growth and break are two scalar parameters on a masked ice material. Mist uses six-way lit flipbooks.
notes: Forgecraft reads as construction. Six forged stakes rise in a sweep, then the ice grows between them and iron straps bind each block.
Every slab is a cluster of three faceted crystals shaded with the shared ice material: wrapped light, parallax crack veils and a frost mask.
The broken segment is alpha clipped to a ragged stump in one frame. Its strap stays hanging between the stakes.
The volley is forty instanced shards flying point first. They stick in the floor where they land and stay as residue, while chunks bounce and settle near the stump.
The attacker is a stage actor that lunges, takes the volley and is thrown back, so the retaliation has a clear cause and effect.

name: Condensation Shield
src: Condensed moisture into a floating disc of ice that acted as a shield. Removed in 0.18.
blurb: Moisture beads out of the air into a trembling lens of water, flash freezes into a floating disc of ice, and takes a hit that leaves a star crack in it.
port: One translucent material with refraction and a Freeze scalar that blends a water normal and an ice layer with frost opacity. Niagara handles droplets, vapour and chips. The crack is a decal style mask positioned at the hit location in disc space.
notes: The disc is a translucent lathe mesh that writes into the distortion buffer, so the caster is seen bent through it. Water bends more, ice less and with a frosted rim.
Condensation is shown as droplets streaking inward to the plane of the disc. The lens wobbles while it is liquid and locks rigid at the freeze.
The freeze front runs from the rim to the centre as a noise threshold. Behind it, radial needle frost and dendrites come from the crack channel of the noise sheet.
A thrown stone tests the shield late in the loop. The disc flashes, sheds chips and keeps a star crack, which is the residue of this piece.
Vapour pours off the lower rim and sinks, and small icicles grow under the disc after the freeze.

name: Ice Form
src: Transformed the caster into a creature of living ice with freezing attacks. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: Frost climbs the caster from the boots up, the body swells into plated ice and sprouts crystal spines, then cracks its rime shell off and stands breathing cold.
port: Character material with a Transform scalar: height masked lerp to an ice layer plus world position offset from a cell texture. Spines are socketed meshes scaled by the same scalar. Shell burst and mist are Niagara emitters sampling the skeletal mesh surface.
notes: The body is the mannequin mesh with a custom material. A noise threshold climbs with height and swaps armour for the shared ice shader.
Behind the front the vertices are pushed out by a 3D cell pattern, so the smooth body turns into bulky plates. Normals switch to screen derivative facets.
Spines are instanced crystals placed on the body surface. Each one grows with an overshoot when the front reaches its height, largest on the shoulders and back.
The snap is the beat: the form swells ten percent, a spiked rim flashes for two frames and the loose rime shell bursts off as chips and powder.
Afterwards the only glow is a slow pulse in the chest and the visor. Mist is born on the body and falls, and frost spreads on the floor around the feet.

name: Bolt of Cold
src: Fired a penetrating bolt of freezing cold that damaged every creature in its path. Removed in 0.25.
blurb: A hair thin lance of cold crosses the room in a few frames, passes through two bodies, and leaves a hanging tube of frozen air and a fan of rime spikes on each back.
port: Niagara beam emitter for the core with a two frame lifetime, spawn per unit along the beam for mist and crystals, and a line trace that returns every hit so each body gets a ring, a material frost event and a socketed spike cluster.
notes: The bolt itself is almost nothing: a white core two centimetres wide that exists for a quarter of a second. Everything else is what the cold does to the air and the bodies.
Penetration is shown three ways. A hard ring snaps open at each body, frost blooms on the chest and the back, and a fan of instanced ice spikes grows out of each back along the path.
The air along the path condenses. Lit mist is born at the moment the head passes each point, hangs as a tube, then sinks and frosts a stripe on the floor.
A travelling light follows the head, so the floor, columns and both targets are swept by cold light in sequence.

name: Absolute Zero
src: Instantly froze the nearest monster solid, killing it outright and leaving a block of ice. Removed in 0.27.
blurb: The light around the victim dies, a ring closes on the floor, and in one frame the creature is inside a jagged block of ice that creaks and pours mist across the stones.
port: Translucent ice material with refraction and a depth fade for the monolith, opaque instanced prisms at the foot, a decal for the frost and Niagara for mist. The light sink is a negative intensity light or a darkening post volume on the victim.
notes: The tell removes energy. A dark alpha volume dims the victim, the effect lights are off and a thin ring contracts on the floor. Nothing glows until the snap.
The freeze has no travel time. The block is present on the first frame, pops by a few percent over two frames, and a tall hard spike of white holds for that long.
The monolith is drawn translucent with refraction, so the victim stays visible as a dark shape bent by the facets. The smaller prisms around its foot are opaque ice.
Aftermath is slow: mist rolls down the faces and along the floor, frost creeps outward, and two settling cracks flash inside the block.

name: Glaciate
src: Blasted a huge cone of ice that damaged and slowed everything inside, freezing the slain into ice blocks. Removed in 0.25.
blurb: A cone of freezing wind tears out of the caster, plants a field of leaning ice spikes and locks the victim inside a growing block of ice.
port: Niagara: mesh renderer for spikes and shards driven by a cone front scalar, six-way lit flipbooks for the wind, a translucent refractive material for the block with a height mask, and a decal for the frost sheet.
notes: The cone is one function of distance from the hand. The frost sheet, the spike growth and the wind all key off the same advancing front.
Spikes are instanced crystal meshes with a faceted ice material. They lean with the blast and pop up with an overshoot as the front passes.
The ice block is an alpha layer with screen refraction that climbs the victim from the floor, so the body stays readable inside it.
Wind is lit mist plus fast ice grit. The only emissive element is a three frame white wedge on the release frame.

name: Poisonous Vapours
src: Turns the air around a target into poison gas for one turn, poisoning it.
blurb: The air around the helmet shimmers, turns in place into a clot of yellow-green gas, then slumps down the shoulders and leaves a wet film and drips.
port: Unreal: a small heterogeneous volume or a ray marched material on a bounding sphere attached to the head socket, with a wetness overlay material parameter on the character and a Niagara drip emitter sampling the skeletal mesh.
notes: Nothing is thrown. The tell is a tightening refraction shimmer and a few motes drawn in, so the gas reads as the air itself changing.
The gas is a 40 step raymarch through the 3D noise volume with one shadow tap toward the key light, clipped against scene depth so the helmet sits inside it.
It is heavy: the volume stretches downward over time while its erosion threshold climbs, so it drains off the head instead of fading.
Residue is a glossy tinted film on the helmet and pauldrons, drips that fall under gravity and spots on the floor.

name: Blue streak
src: The caster dashes at a nearby enemy and makes a melee attack with bonus electric damage based on distance charged.
blurb: The caster gathers static, crosses the room in a tenth of a second as a streak of lightning and lands a blow that throws the target back and burns a line into the floor.
port: Unreal: a root motion dash with a Niagara system attached to the character, ghost trail meshes spawned from pose snapshots, a beam emitter anchored at the start location and a decal spline for the burnt track.
notes: The stage actor really moves. The same closed-form dash curve drives the actor, the lights and every layer, so nothing drifts out of sync.
During the dash the body is replaced in the eye by additive afterimage shells and a multi-filament bolt strung from the start point to the moving chest, with a refraction band for the warped space.
The hit is a hard pale crescent held for three frames, then sparks thrown along the direction of travel and static crawling over the knocked back target.
The floor keeps a burnt track with crack lines that glow and cool, and thin smoke lifts off it.

name: Chain Lightning
src: Releases a huge electrical discharge that arcs from the nearest creature outward to others.
blurb: A dim leader gropes from the hand to the nearest foe, then the return stroke lights the whole tree at once and restrikes twice down the same channel.
port: Niagara beams along a spline array built on the CPU from the target list, with one fixed jitter seed per cast. Leader and return stroke are two emitters on the same spline. Channel vapour is a ribbon or sprite emitter that samples the spline once at spawn.
notes: It is built like real lightning. A faint stepped leader finds the path first, and the bright return stroke then follows exactly that path because both use the same seed.
The tree is five links: hand to the nearest foe, on to two more, and from those into the floor. Each generation fires fifty milliseconds late and a little dimmer.
Three strokes share the channel. Only a thin second strand and the side forks are reseeded per stroke, so the strobe reads as restrikes and not as wobble.
When the light is gone the channel stays behind as a thread of lit vapour that drifts up and shears apart, sampled from the same path function.

name: Airstrike
src: Strikes a creature with a vortex of air, doing more damage when it is surrounded by empty space.
blurb: The air over an exposed enemy winds itself into a funnel, drops, and bursts at the floor. You see it only by the dust it drags and the light it bends.
port: Niagara: a cylinder mesh with a panning erosion material and scene colour refraction for the funnel, ribbon emitters on a helix, mesh particles for the grit with collision. The scour is a decal revealed by a radial mask.
notes: Air has no colour, so the spell is drawn with what air moves: floor dust spiralling in, condensation streaks on the funnel wall, refraction, and grit.
The funnel is a tube mesh with a radius profile set in the vertex shader. It is revealed from the top down, so it reads as descending on the target.
The impact frame is three hard white crescents, built on the arc mesh and held for three frames while they spin outward.
Seventy lit pebbles are dragged a quarter turn inward during the wind up, then thrown out on ballistic arcs and left where they land.

name: Flight
src: Let the caster fly over obstacles for a while (earlier called Fly). Removed in 0.17.
blurb: Dust is drawn to the caster\'s feet, a downwash slaps the floor clean, and the body rises on a column of turning air while grit is flung out and left where it lands.
port: Animate the character root from a curve. Niagara ribbons on helical paths with a refractive haze material, a radial dust burst plus looping ground-hugging dust, a decal for the swept floor and mesh particles with collision for the grit.
notes: The actor is moved by the effect: a short gather, an eased rise and a slow bob driven from the same curve the shaders use.
The downwash is read on the floor. A swept disc, a pale berm of pushed dust and radial streaks appear at liftoff and stay.
Lift is shown with matter, not glow: camera-facing haze ribbons spiral up the body, with motes and refraction rings dropping from the feet.
Pebbles are instanced lit rocks that spiral up, are thrown outward and settle on the flagstones as residue.

name: Deflect Missiles
src: Surrounded the caster with a strong ward that knocked aside most incoming projectiles. Removed in 0.25.
blurb: A fast wall of wind stands up around the caster and a volley of crossbow quarrels is slapped out of the air one after another, each sent tumbling to clatter across the flagstones.
port: Tube mesh with panning streak textures and refraction for the wall. Missiles are mesh particles with a collision event against the ward that swaps velocity to the tangent and enables tumble plus floor collision. Crescents are single-frame sprites spawned from the event.
notes: The barrier is a flared tube with two layers of fast horizontal streaks, refraction and grit carried round in it. It is hard and quick where Repel Missiles is slow and faint.
Five quarrels are instanced lathed meshes. Each flies straight to its own contact point, then takes the wind tangent as its new velocity, tumbles, bounces once and stays on the floor.
Every contact gets a hard white crescent along the wind direction for three frames, a ripple and a lit puff of torn air.
The floor keeps the story: a scoured ring where the wall stands and five spent quarrels lying where they came to rest.

name: Orb of Electrocution
src: Hurled a large orb of lightning that exploded in a burst of electricity. Removed in 0.1 (replaced by Chain Lightning).
blurb: A sphere of ball lightning swells over the raised hand, drifts across the room dragging arcs along the floor, then lets go all at once in a crown of ground strikes.
port: Sphere mesh with a panning filament mask, fresnel rim and refraction. Arcs are beam emitters to line-traced floor points with a pulse curve. Scorch is a decal with an emissive cooling scalar, plus mesh or sprite sparks with collision.
notes: The orb is mostly empty: a refracting shell with a thin rim, a few hairline filaments that reshuffle every other frame and a small white core.
While it travels, stray arcs reach down to the flagstones and leave a dotted line of scorch under the flight path.
The detonation is fourteen instanced strips from the burst point to the floor and the target, pulsed four times with new shapes, under a hard shell ring held for three frames.
The floor keeps a soot star with veins that cool from white to dull orange, and smoke rises off it and off the target.

name: Tornado
src: Surrounded the caster with a huge whirling vortex of wind that battered and flung everything nearby. Removed in 0.27.
blurb: A lit, raymarched funnel of dust winds up around the caster, hauls rubble and a bystander off the floor, then lets go.
port: Niagara: a heterogeneous volume or a stack of lit flipbook cards on a funnel mesh, mesh-renderer debris with a vortex force and collision, and a physics impulse on the ragdoll. Static flicker is a light with a curve, not a sprite.
notes: The funnel is a hollow shell of density raymarched from the 3D noise sheet in twisted coordinates, with one extra sample toward the key light for self shadowing.
Rubble is instanced lit rock on closed-form orbits. When the wind dies each piece leaves on its tangent, falls, bounces once and stays.
The bystander is a stage actor driven by the same orbit maths, thrown clear on release and left lying where he lands.
The only emissive element is a few frames of static inside the funnel, which lights the volume from within.

name: Sandblast
src: Blasts a target with high-velocity rock shards at short range.
blurb: Grit is pulled off the floor into the hand and thrown as a point-blank cone that scours the target and leaves a sand shadow behind him.
port: Niagara: one cone emitter with three renderers (velocity-aligned sprites, six-way lit smoke, mesh shards with collision). The fan is a decal with a mask captured from the target position.
notes: The jet is three scales of matter on one cone: stretched lit grains, soft sand cloud, and a few dozen instanced rock shards that ricochet off the body and stay on the floor.
Core grains stop at the target plane and scatter. Outer grains miss and fly on with drag, so the cone visibly wraps the figure.
The floor decal is a sand fan with a clean wedge behind the target, the stencil a real blast would leave.
Impact is a hard pale crescent for three frames. Everything else is unlit matter catching a small amber light.

name: Granite
src: Launches a huge boulder that rolls in a chosen direction, crushing and pushing back creatures.
blurb: Flagstones tear loose and pack into a boulder that rocks back, barrels across the floor, flattens a man and then falls apart where its magic runs out.
port: Chaos or a baked geometry cache for the break-up, a rolling static mesh on a spline before that. The track is a runtime virtual texture or a decal strip written by the contact point; dust is six-way lit smoke spawned by distance.
notes: The boulder is one lit rock mesh whose roll angle is derived from distance travelled, so it never slides.
Binding cracks glow while the spell holds it together. They flare once more just before it slumps into instanced rubble that stays as a pile.
The floor keeps the story: a torn pit at the source, a crushed track revealed behind the contact point, shed chips along the route.
The target is a stage actor on a damped push with a topple, and the hit frame is a hard forward fan of wedges held for three frames.

name: Tar pit
src: Liquefies the ground in a shrinking radius around the caster, slowing movement through it.
blurb: An alchemical front runs out along the flagstones and the floor behind it slumps into heavy mud that swallows paving and a man to the thigh, then dries from the rim inward.
port: A tessellated or virtual-heightfield mesh with a mud material (two panning normal maps, low roughness), a radius material parameter and a second decal for the crust. Slabs are Niagara mesh particles with a buoyancy curve; bubbles are small lit sprites or a flipbook.
notes: The mud is a displaced, alpha-blended ground mesh shaded as a wet dielectric, so it picks up the stage reflection and the effect lights. Its height field drives both the vertices and the normal.
Loose flagstones are instanced boxes that appear as the front passes, tip on a random axis and go under at their own pace.
The bystander is a stage actor lowered through the surface, which is cheap and reads immediately as depth.
The radius shrinks as in the game. What it leaves is a paler cracked crust, so the full extent of the spell stays written on the floor.

name: Tomb of Doroklohe
src: Sealed the caster inside a tomb of solid rock walls. Removed in 0.3.
blurb: Fissures trace a square around the caster, then eight rough-hewn monoliths punch up out of the floor one after another, far side first, until the last one shuts the caster in.
port: Eight static meshes on a timeline with an overshoot curve, or one Niagara mesh emitter with a spawn order attribute. Use Chaos or a debris emitter at each base. The fissure glow is a decal with an emissive mask that is killed on the seal event.
notes: The eight slabs are one instanced four-sided lathe. A per-vertex hash pushes every ring of vertices around, so each monolith is hewn differently and catches the light in facets.
Eruption order is sorted by distance from the camera, so the caster stays visible until the final slab closes the view.
Each slab overshoots and drops back, throws its own instanced rubble and dust, and leaves a collar of broken soil at its foot.
The spell light sits inside the ring. When the tomb is sealed the light is simply gone, and what remains is dust settling in moonlight.

name: Stoneskin
src: Hardened the caster's skin to stone for extra armour. Removed in 0.18.
blurb: Grit skates in across the floor and climbs the body, setting into cracked stone plates from the boots up before the whole shell clenches tight and sheds its loose flakes.
port: A character material function with a world-aligned voronoi plate mask, a height parameter and WPO. Niagara samples the skeletal mesh surface for the accretion targets and the shed flakes. The rim flash is an overlay material on a timeline.
notes: The mannequin is redrawn with a custom material. A 3D voronoi field makes plates with dark seams, per-plate tilt and a few millimetres of vertex displacement so the shell has thickness.
The stone front is a height threshold warped by noise. Seams glow in the ember tint only within a hand of the front, so the saturated accent stays small.
Grit is pulled from a ring on the floor along bezier paths onto the body surface near the current front, which is where the new stone visibly comes from.
The set beat is a three-frame rim flash on the silhouette, then dust and instanced flakes fall away and stay on the floor.

name: Statue Form
src: Transformed the caster into a slow, heavily armoured living statue. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: Granite climbs the body from the floor behind a thin hot seam, sets with a heavy jolt that cracks the flagstones, and the finished statue grinds its head round.
port: A material layer blend on the character driven by one scalar plus a world-space noise mask. Flakes are a Niagara mesh emitter sampling the skeletal mesh surface with collision; the crack is a deferred decal.
notes: The body is one mesh with two materials. A noisy height threshold swaps armour for speckled granite and the front carries a narrow emissive seam.
The stone half blends toward faceted normals so it reads as chiselled rock rather than painted metal.
Seventy crust flakes are instanced rock meshes released as the front passes them. They fall, land and stay on the floor.
The set frame is a hard pale ring held for a few frames, a low dust skirt and a crack decal under the feet. After that only the eyes glow.

name: Orb of Fragmentation
src: Linley's Crawl earth spell that hurled an orb which burst into a blast of metal fragments. Removed in Linley's 4.0 beta.
blurb: A fist-sized ball of dark iron crosses the room with its seams glowing, then bursts into a fan of blades that bury themselves in the flagstones.
port: Niagara mesh renderer with velocity-aligned orientation and a collision event that kills motion and spawns a stuck mesh. The orb is a material with a cell-border emissive driven by a charge scalar.
notes: The orb is a lit metal sphere whose plates come from a 3D voronoi. The plate borders heat up in flight so the break is announced before it happens.
The burst is a white spiked shape held for two frames. Everything after it is matter: 120 instanced steel blades on ballistic arcs.
Blades fly point first along their velocity and stop dead where they meet the floor, tilted at the entry angle and half buried.
A small dark smoke knot and gouge marks stay behind. The only saturated colour is the heat in the seams and on fresh edges.

name: Blue vitriol
src: Builds a walking alchemical construct that fights, vents toxic clouds and eventually dispenses potions to allies.
blurb: A brass tripod unfolds from a hot ring on the floor, a flask is blown into its cradle and filled, and the finished still stumps forward, belches fumes and throws a punch.
port: A small skeletal mesh with a control rig for the tripod gait and an assembly montage. Glass and liquid are two materials with a fill scalar; fumes and forge sparks are Niagara emitters on sockets.
notes: The whole construct is three instanced layers: cylinders stretched between joint positions, spheres on the joints and rebuilt tori for rings and coil. One set of GLSL joint functions drives all of them.
Assembly is staged per part with overshoot. The flask inflates white hot like blown glass and cools clear before the liquid rises in it.
The liquid is an inner flask clipped at a sloshing level with rising bubble noise. The glass over it is fresnel and environment reflection only.
Legs lift in sequence with a body bob, the near arm winds up and drives through, and the spout vents lit fumes on the punch.

name: Fulsome Fusillade
src: For several turns, rains exploding beakers of random elements on enemies, with overlapping blasts reacting for extra damage.
blurb: Corked glass beakers tumble out of the dark and burst one after another in fire, venom, lightning and frost, ending with two that land together and react.
port: One Niagara system per reagent spawned from a data-driven projectile event, with a shared glass shatter mesh emitter. The residue is a decal chosen by reagent. The reaction is a gameplay event that swaps in a steam burst when two impact radii overlap.
notes: Seven instanced flasks share one timeline function. Each has its own impact time, target and reagent, and every other layer indexes the same function so glass, burst, smoke and stain stay in step.
Each reagent gets a different material answer: blackbody fire with soot, a heavy green gas that hugs the floor, hair thin arcs with a fern scorch, and pale mist with ice chips and frost.
Glass and ice shards are lit instanced meshes on ballistic arcs with one bounce. They stay where they land, next to the scorch, puddle or frost patch.
The last two beakers land on the same spot. Fire meeting frost gives a larger white steam burst and the only full size graphic flash in the piece.

name: Soul Splinter
src: Tears a fragment of a creature's soul out as a fragile soul wisp ally that attacks it, weakening the victim.
blurb: A thread pulls taut, the victim is dragged half out of its own body, and the torn piece snaps free as a small cold flame that turns and bites its former owner.
port: Niagara: the shell is an overlay material on the skeletal mesh with a world position offset driven by one curve. The tether is a two-point ribbon. The wisp is a small flipbook flame with an attached point light and a simple seek behaviour.
notes: The tear is the mannequin mesh drawn again as a rim-lit shell and pushed toward the caster in the vertex shader, strongest at the chest, then let go.
The tether is an analytic ribbon between the chest and the wisp. It thins as it stretches and erodes from the middle when it snaps.
The wisp carries the only strong light in the scene, so the armour, the mist and the floor show where it is at every moment.
Residue is a pale cracked scar on the breastplate and cold mist that spills from it and settles on the floor.

name: Grave Claw
src: Skewers a target with bone shards that never miss and pin it in place, using limited charges gained from kills.
blurb: The floor splits under the victim and six curved talons of old bone punch up through it, close like a hand and hold the body off the ground.
port: Niagara mesh renderer with six talon instances driven by a spline bend in the material, or a small skeletal mesh with a pose asset for hero use. Rubble uses collision. The floor damage is a deferred decal with a crack mask.
notes: Each talon is one lathe mesh bent along a circular arc in the vertex shader, so the same mesh gives six different hooked fingers and a ring of straight splinters.
The talons are staggered by a frame each and overshoot, which reads as a hand closing. They are clipped at the floor plane so they appear to come through it.
Bone is a lit material: ivory with brown grime in the cracks, soil at the base and a dark wet stain near the tips.
The floor keeps the evidence: a churned dark patch, radial cracks, thrown rubble that bounces once and stays, and dust that hangs in the flash light.

name: Grave green
src: Makes the caster nearly invulnerable for a brief time while reducing them to the brink of death.
blurb: A ruined stone doorway rises behind the caster and swings open onto a black-violet void, the caster\'s colour is drawn into it until they stand pale as a corpse, and arrows pass straight through them in puffs of grave mist.
port: Modular stone door meshes with a height dissolve, a translucent void material with a twirl panner and refraction, a character material lerp to a pallid preset, and projectile actors with pass-through collision that spawn a Niagara mist burst.
notes: The doorway is six lit stone boxes alpha-clipped up from the floor with a violet build edge, then a void plane opens from a slit with a ragged rim, twirled smoke and a cold light far inside it.
The caster is a custom mannequin layer whose armour drains to a rough, desaturated corpse white from the chest outward while warm motes stream off the body into the door.
A light sink on the caster and a violet light from the door do most of the mood work. The open frame has a two-frame hard outline flash.
Invulnerability is shown, not told: three arrows on real ballistic arcs fly through the body, the ghost shell ripples where they pass, and they end up stuck in the floor behind.

name: Twisted Resurrection
src: Fused corpses in view into shambling abominations under the caster's control. Removed in 0.16.
blurb: Cords of dark energy drag four corpses across the floor in jerks, the pile swells, and a stitched mass of mismatched flesh and armour stands up out of it.
port: Corpses are skeletal meshes moved by a timeline with a decal trail. The abomination is an authored mesh revealed with a scale and morph curve; the patch and seam look is a material using a 3D cellular texture. Gore uses Niagara mesh droplets with collision decals.
notes: The corpses are instanced mannequin meshes laid flat. They are pulled in three hard yanks with rests between, and each leaves a wet smear along its path.

The abomination is a solid raymarched form: ellipsoids and capsules blended with smooth minimum, so torsos, heads and spare arms melt into one body. It writes depth, so drops and smoke sort against it.
Its surface is cut into patches by 3D voronoi. Each patch takes a different dead flesh tone or an armour plate, and the borders become dark seams with stitch marks and a dying glow.
Residue is the drag smears, the pool that spreads under the mass, and the gore thrown out at the moment it stands.

name: Gloom
src: Emits a wave of gloom that may blind nearby living, demonic or holy creatures.
blurb: The caster inhales the light of the room, then exhales a rolling ring of ink that snuffs the braziers one by one and leaves everyone it touched with a rag of shadow bound over their eyes.
port: Point lights with a timeline curve per brazier and a negative light or post-process darkening volume for the sink. The ring is a Niagara emitter with a radial velocity and a roll vortex, the soot a growing decal, and the shroud a skinned cloth mesh with a dissolve material.
notes: Darkness is the effect. The two brazier lights lean toward the caster during the tell, then go out the moment the wave front reaches them, while a growing negative light sinks the middle of the room.
The impact frame is a negative graphic: a spiked black burst with a thin violet rim, held for three frames.
The wave is a ring of lit dark smoke puffs that roll forward around a travelling core, with a soot decal following the front so the floor stays dimmer behind it.
Each bystander flinches as the front passes and a torn band of shadow cloth knits itself around the visor. Snuffed braziers keep smoking from cooling coals.

name: Cause Fear
src: Frightens nearby creatures that fail a willpower check so they cannot approach the caster and may fail to attack.
blurb: The light drains from the room, a towering smoke shade rears up behind the caster, and its opening eyes drive the foes skidding backwards.
port: Author the shade as a lit volumetric flipbook or a heterogeneous volume, with eyes as emissive cards. The recoil is an animation notify on the victims, and the light drain is a negative light or a post-process exposure dip in a sphere mask.
notes: Fear is staged with darkness. A negative point light empties the floor around the caster during the tell, so the pale eye light that follows hits hard.
The shade is a raymarched smoke volume shaped by a hooded figure with two reaching arms. A shadow tap toward the key light gives it a lit rim and a black core.
The impact frame is inverted: a black spiked burst with a thin pale rim, held for three frames.
The foes are stage actors that recoil, lean away and tremble. Their shadows are stretched away from the shade and their heels leave pale skid marks and dust.

name: Dimensional Bullseye
src: Links the caster's projectiles to a target so each shot at another enemy also teleports a copy at the target.
blurb: A reticle of bent space locks onto one foe, and every bolt thrown at its neighbour is echoed out of a small rift and buried in the marked one.
port: Reticle as a translucent material with scene-colour refraction on a camera-facing card. Bolts are mesh particles with a clip plane parameter, and the rifts are small portal cards with a cubemap interior.
notes: Two foes make the rule readable: the caster shoots the far one, and a twin bolt leaves a rift beside the marked one a few frames later.
The reticle is mostly refraction. Thin rings and ticks are drawn with screen-space derivatives, and the lens inside them magnifies the armour behind.
Bolts are lit steel meshes that stay embedded after the hit. The copies are clipped against the rift plane, so they slide out of nothing.
A hard hairline joins the bolt in flight to its rift for two frames. The rift then closes into a jagged scar of light that fades slowly.

name: Bog
src: Summons a crocodile beneath the caster that attacks an adjacent enemy and drags it and the caster backward.
blurb: Black water wells up under the caster\'s boots, a crocodile explodes out of it in a sheet of spray, clamps the enemy across the waist and hauls everyone back toward the pool before sinking away.
port: Skeletal mesh crocodile with a root-motion lunge and drag montage; the victim is attached to a jaw socket for the drag. Water uses a translucent decal with a ripple normal flipbook, Niagara droplets with collision and a wet-surface decal spawned along the drag spline.
notes: The pool is a floor decal with an environment reflection on rippled normals; the crocodile is a raymarched solid whose body is a capsule anchored below the floor, so the opaque floor hides everything under the waterline for free.
One pose function in GLSL drives skull position, pitch and jaw angle. The JavaScript actors mirror it, so the victim slides exactly with the snout and the caster is shoved back by the surge.
The bite frame is a pair of hard white jaw crescents snapping shut for two frames, then the matter takes over: ballistic droplets, a lit spray cloud and drips from the jaws.
Residue: a wet drag streak across the flagstones with a specular sheen, puddles beading round the pool and a ring of ripples after the crocodile sinks.

name: Summon Cactus Giant
src: Summons a cactus giant ally whose spines hurt melee attackers.
blurb: Sand spins up out of the flagstones, the floor bursts, and a ribbed saguaro giant twice the height of the caster shoulders its way up through the pile, bristling with bone-pale spines.
port: A skeletal mesh with a rise animation and a spine card or mesh layer. Sand uses Niagara with six-way lit flipbooks, a mesh mound with a growth morph and a spray decal. The fluting can be a normal map and tessellated displacement.
notes: The giant is a solid raymarched body made of ribbed capsules. The fluting is in the distance field, so the ribs catch real light and the silhouette is scalloped.
Spines are 340 instanced needle meshes placed on the rib crests of the same capsule list the distance field uses, so they stay glued to the body as it rises.
Sand is the physical evidence: a vortex tell, a lit dust eruption, streams pouring off the shoulders as it rises, and a mound and spray pattern that stay on the floor.
Colour is dusty green and sand. The one saturated accent is the blossom that opens on the crown and arm at the end.

name: Malign Gateway
src: Opens a temporary portal from which a huge eldritch tentacle emerges to fight, turning hostile when the portal expires.
blurb: A ragged gash tears open in the air, a black tentacle freckled with cold stars hauls itself out, rears, and whips down into the flagstones beside the foe before thrashing and slithering back as the wound seals.
port: Skeletal tentacle mesh with a spline IK or a Niagara ribbon-to-mesh deform, and a clip plane in the material at the portal. The gash is a translucent card with a parallax starfield material; the slam is a Niagara burst with mesh debris and six-way lit dust.
notes: The tentacle is a 64-row tube swept along a cubic curve whose tip is animated through emerge, rear, slam and thrash poses. Retracting simply shortens the curve, so it slides back along its own path.
Fragments behind the portal plane are clipped, so the limb always appears to come out of the gash and not from behind it.
The skin is near-black wet hide with pale suckers on the underside and tiny twinkling stars on the back, which carries the eldritch read without a neon fill.
The slam is the impact frame: a hard spiked flash, rock chunks that bounce and stay, lit dust and a cracked, ichor-wet crater left behind.

name: Summon Guardian Golem
src: Summoned a golem that absorbed damage dealt to the caster's allies and exploded when overloaded. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: Rubble flies in and stacks into a squat iron-banded golem that drinks its allies wounds down pale tethers until its cracks run white and it bursts.
port: Unreal: a skeletal golem with a dissolve plane and an emissive crack mask driven by a heat parameter. Tethers are Niagara ribbons with a travelling pulse in the material, and the burst swaps to a Chaos or mesh-particle debris system with six-way lit dust.
notes: The golem is a sphere-traced SDF written as a solid ray layer, cut by a rising plane during assembly so it builds from the feet while instanced rocks arc in to meet the cut.
Each wound is a spark on an ally that becomes a pulse racing down a sagging tether. Every arrival raises one heat scalar that opens blackbody cracks in the stone.
Overload is one frame: the body is cut down to a broken stump, the same rock instances switch to a ballistic burst with one bounce, and a hard ring flash holds for two frames.
Residue: the leg stumps stay standing, hot fragments cool on the floor and lit dust hangs in the air.

name: Monstrous Menagerie
src: Summoned one or more mythical beasts such as manticores, lindwurms or a sphinx. Removed in 0.33.
blurb: A scratched ochre circle opens into a pit of sand-coloured light and a manticore hauls itself out, lands hard and stands over the cooling sigil with its sting raised.
port: In Unreal the beast is a skeletal mesh with a spawn montage and the pit is a decal with a depth-fade card under it. Dust uses six-way lit flipbooks, rim chips are a Niagara mesh emitter with collision, and the sigil is an emissive decal whose reveal angle and heat are two scalar curves.
notes: The beast is one signed distance field: ellipsoids and tapered capsules blended with smooth minimum, marched inside a bounding sphere and written to the depth buffer so dust and debris sort against it.
Its fur is a bumped normal and a streaked albedo from the 3D noise volume, lit by shade() with a four-tap ambient occlusion so the belly and the leg pits go dark.
The rig is driven by one lunge scalar: the body pitches up out of the pit, the forelegs reach, and everything settles with a damped bounce when the paws land.
The pit is only a decal. The floor depth clips the body, which is all the eye needs to read a creature climbing out of a hole.
Residue: the sigil cools to pale scratches in the flagstones, rim chips stay where they bounced and the dust hangs in the moonlight.

name: Dispersal
src: Teleports or blinks away all creatures near the caster.
blurb: The caster draws the air in, then throws space outward: three surrounding foes collapse into slits of light and are dropped across the room in puffs of displaced dust.
port: Niagara: a character-surface emitter with a point attractor on the root for the implosion, a mesh renderer with collision for pebbles and a screen-space refraction sphere for the shell. The teleport itself is gameplay; the effect only needs the two world positions per victim.
notes: The tell is an inhale. A refractive shell contracts on the caster while floor grit creeps inward, so the release has something to push against.
Each foe vanishes as a body shell that collapses onto its own axis and a two-frame vertical slit. Dust spawned on the body surface is sucked into the gap the body left.
Arrivals are the reverse: a slit, an outward ring of lit dust and a staggering body. The lights jump from the old positions to the new ones.
The shock sweeps the flagstones. Pebbles are real instanced meshes that hop outward and stay, and pale radial dust streaks remain as residue.

name: Sandstone hall
src: Reorients gravity in a chosen direction, making all creatures in sight tumble that way and collide with obstacles.
blurb: Down becomes sideways: a hanging censer swings level, rubble and two armoured bodies fall across the floor into a wall, hang there, then drop when gravity is given back.
port: In engine this is a gameplay gravity override on physics bodies plus a Niagara system that reads the gravity vector as a user parameter for dust and smoke. The censer is a physics constraint; the lurch is a one-shot post-process shear.
notes: The read comes from a plumb line. A censer on a chain swings to horizontal and its smoke streams the other way, so the new direction of down is never in doubt.
Bodies and rubble use the same sideways free fall, x equals half g t squared, so everything arrives at the wall on one accelerating beat.
Impacts are a three-frame spiked flash on the wall face, a crack decal that stays, and dust that is thrown off the wall and then pulled back onto it.
When the spell ends the pinned rocks and bodies drop under normal gravity. The rubble heap at the foot of the wall is the residue.

name: Portal
src: Opened a magical portal that carried the caster to another level of the dungeon. Removed in 0.8.
blurb: The flagstones under the caster lift and part, a shaft of turning light opens straight down through the floor, and the caster drops into it before the hole snaps shut on a ring of fused stone.
port: Material on a floor decal with a bump offset or a cylinder mesh below a stencil mask for the shaft. Slabs are a Niagara mesh emitter with a vortex force and a kill volume, the rest are standard lit flipbooks.
notes: The well is a ray layer: each pixel inside the opening is traced down a virtual cylinder below the floor, so the spiral bands have real depth and parallax as the camera moves.
Tell: a scratched circle and stress cracks light up while loose slabs rise and hover. The opening is an iris with a little overshoot and a hard floor ring for two frames.
Slabs inside the circle spiral in and fall down the shaft; slabs outside it drop back when the iris slams shut and stay where they land.
Residue is a fused glassy ring with a pale ash lip, swept dust streaks pointing into the centre and cracks that cool from violet to dark.

name: Singularity
src: Created a gravitational singularity that dragged in and crushed everything in sight. Removed in 0.17.
blurb: A pinhole in the air swells into a lightless sphere ringed by a burning disk of torn stone, drags rubble and bodies inward, then collapses and drops a single fist-sized lump of crushed rock that glows on the floor.
port: Black sphere mesh plus a refraction post material driven by a screen-space vector to the centre. The disk is a flat mesh with a polar panner material. Debris uses a Niagara point attractor with a kill sphere and a second emitter that spawns the core on the collapse event.
notes: The sphere is pure black; the read comes from what surrounds it. A screen-space lens pulls the background toward it and a thin halo stands in for light bent over the top.
The disk is a tilted mesh shaded with Keplerian shear, so the inner edge turns faster and runs hotter. The doppler side is brighter.
Floor rubble is instanced lit rock. Each piece waits its turn, lifts, spirals inward and is squeezed out of existence at the horizon. Whatever is still in flight at the collapse falls where it is.
Two bystanders are dragged across the floor while leaning back against it. The floor keeps radial crush cracks, swept grit and the glowing compacted core.

name: Kinetic Grapnel
src: Fires a grapnel at an enemy that makes the caster's next melee attack on it more accurate and damaging.
blurb: A small forged hook spits from the raised hand on a hair of force, bites into the target with a shower of sparks, then the line snaps taut and yanks the target a stride forward.
port: Niagara: a mesh projectile with a beam emitter between two sockets whose tangents are driven by a damped sine, a spark burst on the hit event and a decal spawned by the root motion of the yank.
notes: The hook is real lit geometry: a steel shank and three prongs that open as it bites. It stays embedded in the armour, still cooling, for the rest of the shot.
The filament is an analytic ribbon. It flies slack with a travelling wave, snaps straight on impact and rings as a decaying standing wave, then rings again on the yank.
Impact gives metal-on-metal sparks with gravity and floor bounce plus a few dark flecks of armour that land and stay.
The yank is the second beat: the target is dragged half a metre and leaves two pale scrape marks and a puff of dust at its heels.

name: Blue hammer
src: A magic hammer strikes one of the caster's constructs, repairing and empowering it and damaging adjacent enemies.
blurb: A spectral sledge assembles from embers above a cracked iron construct, swings back and falls in one stroke; the cracks weld shut, temper colours run down the hull and molten slag spatters the floor while the shock throws back everyone beside it.
port: Construct material with a temper gradient driven by a world-space front parameter and a crack mask that lerps closed. The hammer is a translucent mesh with fresnel emissive and a dissolve. Slag is a Niagara mesh emitter with collision that switches to a flattened splat mesh on impact.
notes: The construct is a lit lathe hull with rivet bands. Before the strike its cracks smoulder and spit; after it a heat front runs down the body, sealing the cracks and leaving real oxide temper bands from straw to bronze to blue.
The hammer is a ghost of a forge tool: dark translucent body with a burning rim, built from embers that converge on it and dissolving back into sparks two frames after the strike.
Impact frame: a hard white ring and a spiked burst, then a floor shock ring, a spark fountain and instanced slag droplets that fly, land, flatten into splats and cool from orange to black crust.
The two adjacent enemies are shoved back and lean away from the blow; the floor keeps a pale shock ring and the cooling splats.

name: Forge Phalanx Beetle
src: Builds a mechanical beetle that stays beside the caster and boosts their armour class.
blurb: Five white-hot forgings fly in and lock into an iron beetle at the caster\'s side, which cools, opens its eyes and lays a plate ward over its maker.
port: Build the beetle as five skeletal mesh parts with a heat material parameter and animate the assembly in Sequencer or a Niagara mesh emitter. The ward is an overlay material on the character driven by one sweep scalar.
notes: The beetle is one solid raymarched SDF made of five parts. Each part has its own arrival time, offset and heat, so the construct visibly assembles instead of fading in.
Heat is a per-part scalar that feeds an emissive ramp and the scene light. Parts arrive glowing and cool to dark hammered iron with brass trim over about two seconds.
Every lock throws a small fan of sparks that fall and bounce. The forge circle under the beetle stays behind as a cooling scorch with a pale ash lip.
The armour bonus is a plate lattice drawn on a shell of the caster mesh. It sweeps up the body once when the last part locks, then settles to a faint rim.

name: Fortress Blast
src: After a delay during which the caster is rooted, releases a large shockwave whose damage is based on the caster\'s armour.
blurb: A ring of stone bulwark slabs grinds up around the rooted caster, then the whole wall is thrown flat by a grey kinetic shockwave that scours the floor.
port: Niagara mesh renderer for the slabs with a scripted two-state motion (rise, then tip and slide), or a Chaos cache for hero shots. The ring is a single mesh with a refraction pass. Dust uses six-way lit flipbooks and the cracks are a deferred decal.
notes: The delay is the wall. Twelve instanced slabs rise one after another while dust creeps inward along the floor and the bastion plan under the caster brightens.
Release is a single hard white ring held for three frames, with a wider refraction ring behind it. No fire: the blast is pressure, dust and thrown stone.
Each slab tips outward about its base and slides to rest, so the wall ends as a sunburst of fallen stone. Rubble bounces once and stays.
Dust is lit sprites in two layers: a fast ground front that follows the wave and a slow haze that hangs in the moonlight. Radial cracks keep a pale lip so they read on the dark floor.

name: Platinum Paragon
src: Builds a powerful metal champion wielding a copy of the caster\'s weapon; it can later be overloaded for a wide flurry of attacks.
blurb: A white-hot platinum knight drops out of the dark onto a forge sigil, cracks the floor, cools to polished metal and then overloads into a four-cut flurry.
port: A skeletal mesh with a heat and charge scalar in its material, landing driven by a Sequencer track. Rubble and sparks are Niagara mesh and sprite emitters with collision, the crescents are four slash meshes with an erode material and the crater is a decal with a cooling emissive curve.
notes: Tell: the caster raises a hand and a rune circle burns into the floor where the champion will land. The fall itself is a third of a second with a thin descent streak above it.

The knight is the stage mannequin with its own material: polished platinum with engraved plate seams, a heat term that starts blackbody white and cools over two seconds, and steam lifting off its surface.
Landing is pressure, not magic: a hard white floor ring for three frames, a refraction ring, thrown rubble that bounces and stays, and a dust skirt lit by the cooling body.

The overload is the second beat. Seams and the replica greatsword charge in the tint, the knight sinks slightly, then four bold crescents cut around it in 0.3 seconds and leave hot gouges in the stone.

name: Beastly Appendage
src: Temporarily grew a beastly body part (horns or talons) for an extra melee attack. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: Feral heat veins the helmet and gauntlets, then keratin horns and hooked talons punch out through the steel in a spray of metal and blood, steaming as they cool.
port: Horn and talon meshes on head and hand sockets with a morph or scale curve and a dissolve-in mask; the armour material gets a vein emissive driven by distance from the sockets. Niagara bursts for splinters (mesh renderer with collision), sparks and steam, plus a spatter decal.
notes: Horns and talons are tube meshes bent along cubic splines in the vertex shader. Growth evaluates the spline only up to a growth scalar with a back-eased overshoot, so they punch out and settle.
The anticipation is in the body material: crack veins crawl outward from the scalp and the hands with an accelerating pulse while the figure trembles.
At the snap the armour gives way: 44 instanced steel splinters fly from the roots on ballistic arcs with one bounce and stay on the floor beside a wet spatter decal.
Fresh keratin carries a cooling orange core near the root and a steam plume, so the growth reads as hot living matter rather than a glowing prop.

name: Blade Hands
src: Transformed the caster's hands into long blades for powerful unarmed attacks. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: Iron filings stream up off the flagstones into the raised hands, steel creeps down the forearms, and two curved blades are drawn out of the fists with a single ringing snap.
port: Blades are static meshes scaled along a spline with a metal material, the forearm creep is a mask in the character material driven by one scalar. Filings are Niagara ribbons with a point attractor, then a collision burst for the fallout.
notes: The steel has a source. Filings are pulled off the floor along arcs into each hand before any metal appears, and the excess is thrown off and falls when the blades lock.
Blades are the sword mesh bent and flared in the vertex shader and grown along their length. They use the metal BRDF and the room reflection, so they read as steel and not as light.
The forearms are re-skinned in the body material: a noise edged front converts armour to polished steel from the fist toward the elbow, with a thin hot seam at the boundary.
The snap is two frames of white along both edges and a four point glint on each tip. Afterwards the caster turns and a slow highlight runs down the blades.

name: Hydra Form
src: Transformed the caster into a many-headed hydra that could devour foes. Removed in 0.27.
blurb: Scales crawl up the caster while the back heaves, then the body splits open and a squat hydra unfolds its necks over a spray of bile and snaps at the air.
port: A skeletal hydra with procedural neck chains (Control Rig spline IK) revealed under a dissolve on the caster mesh. Gobbets are a Niagara mesh emitter that spawns decals on collision, steam is lit flipbook smoke.
notes: Anticipation lives on the caster mesh: a voronoi scale pattern climbs from the boots behind a thin bile seam while lumps heave under the back plates.
The hydra is one solid raymarch: a heavy body, stubby legs, a tail and up to five bezier necks built from capsules, each with a hinged two part jaw.
Each head runs its own snap cycle with a lunge and an open jaw, after a shared rearing roar right after emergence, so the silhouette never freezes.
The split throws instanced gobbets of ichor that flatten into splats where they land. Steam lifts off the new hide and drool falls from the mouths.

name: Dragon Form
src: Transformed the caster into a dragon with powerful attacks and a breath weapon. Removed in 0.31.
blurb: A spiral of fire climbs the caster until the column bursts, and a rearing dragon steps out of it, unfurls its wings and tests its breath across the scorched floor.
port: A skeletal dragon revealed inside a fire column, with an emissive seam mask in its material that cools on a curve. Wings are part of the skeleton with a two sided translucent material. Fire, smoke and breath are Niagara flipbook emitters with a scorch decal.
notes: The tell is combustion with a source: fire licks up from the flagstones in a tightening spiral while the caster chars from the boots up.
The dragon is a solid raymarch with a heavy chest, a bezier neck, a hinged jaw and swept horns. Ember light glows in the scale seams and cools to black over two seconds.
Wings are subdivided planes shaped in the vertex shader with a scalloped trailing edge, bone ribs and light bleeding through the membrane from the fire.
The breath is a short test burst of blackbody flame from the mouth with its own light, so the third beat lights the floor and the scorch it leaves behind.

name: Repel Undead
src: Linley's Crawl holy spell that drove nearby undead away from the caster. Removed in Linley's 4.0 beta.
blurb: A ring of pale gold light rolls out across the floor from a warding priest, shoving three closing corpses back on their heels, scorching them and leaving a scribed ward circle they cannot cross.
port: Corpses are skeletal meshes with a hit reaction driven by the ring radius crossing their distance. The ring is a scaled decal and cylinder mesh from one radius curve. Smoke is a Niagara emitter attached to each corpse, spawned by the same event.
notes: The undead are instanced mannequins with their own bone and rot material and alpha-clipped tears, hunched and shambling in until the ring reaches them.
Each corpse is hit at the exact moment the ring radius passes it. It is shoved outward with drag, rocks back and settles into a cowering lean outside the circle.
The ring is a bright leading edge on the floor with a low wall of light above it. It stops at a fixed radius and cools into a line of scribed runes.
The scorched corpses smoke and shed embers from the side facing the priest, and their cold eye glints gutter out.

name: Greater Healing
src: Restored a large amount of the caster's health. Removed in 0.5.
blurb: A shaft of warm daylight breaks down through the crypt dark onto the caster, lifting them off their feet in a slow storm of lit dust and rising sparks, then sets them down on a circle of floor scoured pale.
port: A light function or volumetric spot for the shaft with a cylinder card for the core, a Niagara dust emitter lit by that light, and a bleach decal for the floor. The lift is a root motion curve with a landing dust burst event.
notes: The column is a soft volume card with a sharp core, opened narrow and widened with a hard ring flash on the floor at full strength.
Most of the read is lit matter: 160 dust motes shaded by the shaft light hang and swirl inside it, and sparks rise from the floor on helical paths.
The body takes the light as a warm fresnel shell that throbs twice like a heartbeat while the actor floats a hand span off the floor.
On landing a low ring of dust puffs out from the feet. The circle the light stood on stays bleached and faintly warm.

name: Brand Weapon With Holy Wrath
src: One-time gift that permanently brands a weapon with holy wrath at an altar.
blurb: A plain sword lifts off a stone altar, turns point down and is swallowed by white-gold fire, then the flame draws itself into the edges of the blade and the branded sword drives itself into the altar.
port: Unreal: the sword is a static mesh with an emissive edge mask driven by a brand parameter; fire and smoke are Niagara ribbons or sprites spawned from a mesh-surface location module. The plant is a sequencer keyframe with a camera-shake-free impulse and a Niagara chip burst.

name: Sign of Ruin
src: Marks a group of enemies around the target so that melee damage against them also drains them and inflicts weakness, blindness or slowness.
blurb: A violet crack runs from the caster to the enemy group, a ring of ashen light bursts across the floor and the ruin mark stamps above every head, where it hangs dripping black smoke.
port: Three world-space sprite meshes with an SDF material and a stamp curve, Niagara drip and smoke emitters on a socket above each marked enemy, a deferred decal for the ring and crack.
notes: The sign is the shared ruin mark distance field: an inked black core with a thin violet burning edge, stamped in at one and a half times scale with a three frame white flash.
Each mark is a light sink as well as a light: a dark smoky halo sits behind it so it reads against the bright floor ring.
Black ichor drips from the lowest thorns as stretched drops, and slower lit smoke trails from them and pools around the shoulders.
The ashen ring is the only near-white light in the piece. It leaves a pale ash deposit and a cooling crack line back to the caster.

name: Receive Forbidden Knowledge
src: One-time gift granting knowledge of Haunt, Borgnjor's Revivification, Infestation and Death's Door (alternative to the pain brand).
blurb: A black grimoire bound with the ruin mark bursts open in a cold wind, its pages riffle and four great glyphs tear loose and pour into the caster, then the spent book slams shut and drops smoking to the floor.
port: A skeletal book mesh with an open and riffle animation, a Niagara ribbon of glyph sprites to a head socket, mesh particles for the four hero glyphs and a physics drop at the end.
notes: The book is a small rig in one GLSL function: two covers and two page blocks hinge on the spine, and eight instanced pages flip across with a curl while the wind holds it open.
Small glyphs stream along curved paths from the pages to the head; four large glyphs, one per granted spell, follow on their own timings so the gift reads as a count.
The impact is the ruin mark flashing over the caster for three frames, after which the visor keeps a faint violet glint.
When the gift is spent the book shuts, falls under gravity, bounces once and lies flat, shedding scorched page scraps and a little smoke.

name: Drain Life
src: Drained life from all living creatures in sight to heal the worshipper (removed in 0.32).
blurb: Wet crimson threads lance from the worshipper into every living thing nearby, pump their colour inward, then snap in one rush that floods the caster.
port: Niagara: ribbon renderer on spline-sampled particles per target, a user parameter for drain progress that also drives the victim material pallor, and a collision event spawning blood decals.
notes: Nine strip meshes follow twisting splines from each victim chest to the caster hands and chest, shaded as wet blood with env() highlights rather than as glow.
Motes ride the splines inward while the victim armour shader drains toward grey and they slump forward on their feet.
At the rush every thread breaks from its middle, the stubs retract, and droplets fall under gravity onto blood decals that stay.
One hard crimson ring holds for three frames around the caster; the heal reads as veins of light running up the body and fading.

name: Receive Weapon
src: One-time gift: choose one weapon from four offered.
blurb: Four weapons descend point-first down shafts of red-gold light over a burning battle sigil; three burn away to gold ash and the chosen blade drives itself into the flagstones at the caster\'s feet.
port: Four weapon meshes on a spline descent driven by one timeline. A dissolve material parameter for the refused ones spawns Niagara ash at the erosion edge. The chosen one ends with a socket on the floor, a decal and a chip burst.
notes: Anticipation: the shield-boss sigil of Okawaru is burned into the floor by one clockwise sweep while four light shafts open and each lights its own pool of floor.
The weapons are real lit meshes: two swords from the sword mesh and a spear and flanged mace reshaped from one cylinder in the vertex shader, all with bronze fittings.
Impact: the refused weapons erode from the point upward into rising gold ash, the chosen one lifts, then slams into the stone with a held eight-point flash, chips and a dust ring.
Residue: the blade stays embedded and quivers to rest, cracks and pale dust ring its foot and the sigil cools to a dull engraved glow.

name: Vessel of Slaughter
src: (Mark of the Fanatic) A damnation explosion surrounds the user, who transforms into a demonic avatar; afterwards they are dragged to the Crucible of Flesh.
blurb: Crimson fractures crawl over the fanatic until the body burns away in a ring of damnation fire, and out of it unfolds a towering obsidian demon with sweeping horns, cracked with hellfire and wreathed in a blood-red haze.
port: Swap the character mesh for the avatar skeletal mesh behind a dissolve on the event frame. The ring is a Niagara radial burst with a ground decal that writes a pass time; the avatar material uses an emissive crack mask with a pulsing scalar and a fresnel aura.
notes: The tell is on the body: crack lines from the shared noise sheet spread up the armour while the Mark of the Fanatic burns under the feet and dark smoke is drawn in around the ankles.
At the impact frame the body is alpha-eroded from the feet up with a burning edge, a barbed seven-point flash holds for two frames and the damnation ring races out across the floor.

The avatar is a solid raymarched form about three metres tall: digitigrade legs, a broad V torso, spiked shoulders, spread clawed arms and long sweeping horns. It unfolds with an overshoot scale and then breathes.
Its obsidian hide is glossy and almost black; the light comes from crimson cracks and a burning chest. Residue is the scorched ring with a pale ash rim, embers and a rising blood-red haze.

name: Brothers in Arms
src: Summons large berserk allies to fight alongside the user.
blurb: Two columns of red-lit dust spin up from the floor, a pair of club-wielding hill giants drop out of them and slam into a crouch, and they surge forward through the settling dust, war paint smeared, glowing with Trog’s rage.
port: Skeletal giants with land and charge montages, spawned by a summoning Blueprint. Dust as six-way lit Niagara smoke, cracks as decals with a growth parameter, chips as a mesh emitter.
notes: The giants share one raymarched map with two transforms: barrel torso, jutting jaw, long arms and a crude club, with bone-tan skin, blood-red war paint and a red fresnel rage rim.
Each lands with a hard slam: cracks and a dust ring, flying floor chips and a light kick, then rises out of the crouch and charges a short way forward with a stride and bob.
The tell is two swirling pillars of red-lit dust, so the arrival has a source and the room is coloured before the impact.
Residue is two cracked landing craters with claw gouges, plus dust that settles behind the charge.

name: Pacify
src: (0.35 trunk) Attempts to soothe a hostile creature so it turns neutral and leaves the level, granting full experience.
blurb: A slow crescent of calm light rolls across the floor from an open palm, snuffs the red rage smoking off a hostile figure, crowns it with a halo, and the figure turns and walks away.
