blurb: A lacquered red and black carousel wheels out under the enemy line, a rusted crown of hooks strings them up like puppets and barbed threads stitch them together, so when a firebolt burns one, the pain runs down the wires and snaps through the others.
port: Niagara ribbons with a sag parameter for the wires and a moving emissive band for the pulse; the crown is a static mesh with a dissolve material. The carousel is a decal using a polar stripe function with a rotation parameter.
notes: Tell: the floor sigil unwinds in a spiral, an iron crown with hanging hooks erodes into being above the group and barbed wires drop from it to every shoulder, then sag between the chests.

Impact: the caster triggers it with an ordinary firebolt. On the hit a crimson bead runs along the links and lands on the neighbours a beat later as a black crescent with a red rim, held for three frames.
The wires are camera-facing strips with a parabolic sag that snaps taut when the pulse passes, and a barbed width profile so they read as wire, not light.
Residue: the burnt target smokes, the wheel keeps turning, the wires keep trembling and blood sprays onto the flagstones under the victims.

name: Drain Pulse
src: Deals dark and poison damage in a large burst around the caster and heals you for half.
blurb: The caster sucks the light out of the room, then slams it outward as a low wall of black, venom-tinged smoke that stains the flagstones, and the blood it tears from every foe streams back into his chest.
port: Niagara: a ring emitter whose radius follows a curve for the smoke wall, and a second emitter that spawns on the victims’ skeletal mesh surfaces with a point attractor for the return. The stain is a decal driven by the same radius curve.
notes: Tell: a negative light dims the floor around the caster while dark motes spiral in and red veins crawl through the stone under his feet.
Impact: a hard crimson ring snaps out for three frames and the shock wall of lit black smoke rolls outward on an ease-out radius; each enemy rocks back the moment the front reaches it.
Two hundred blood droplets peel off each victim’s body surface and fly home on bowed bezier paths, so the healing half reads as a visible return.
Residue: a scorched disc with a pale ash lip at the wave’s furthest reach, sickly venom in its cracks, grey pallor on the victims and a warm pulse in the caster’s armour.

name: Mass Calcification
src: Kills all non-undead allies and raises them as Bone Shamblers that split on death.
blurb: A front of grey chalk crawls across the floor from the caster’s feet; as it reaches each ally their armour and flesh turn to porous bone from the boots up, shed in dark flakes, and they fold over into hunched, spur-backed shamblers.
port: A material function on the character with a world-height mask for the bone swap and a morph target or bone-driven additive pose for the hunch. Spurs are skeletal-socket meshes with a scale curve; the floor crust is a decal driven by a radial gradient parameter.
notes: Tell: grit spins around the caster’s raised hand and a hard pale ring snaps out on the floor, then a chalk front spreads at walking pace, leaving a powdery crust behind it.
Each ally is a custom mannequin layer. A calcification height climbs from the feet with a glowing lip, the material swaps to fissured bone, and a vertex bend folds the spine and knees into a hunch.
Bone spurs are instanced lathe spikes anchored in body space and pushed through the same bend function, so they stay attached while the body slumps; they punch out with an overshoot.
Residue: chalk crust on the floor, dark flakes of shed flesh at every pair of feet, and three swaying bone heaps where the party stood.

name: Soul Tax
src: Deals a third of the target's current HP as holy and dark damage and heals the caster.
blurb: A tithe seal marks a third of the victim, then a braided strand of white light and black smoke is torn out of its chest and reeled into the caster, while the soul falls away as hot tarnished coin.
port: Two Niagara ribbon emitters sharing a spline with a phase offset; the coins are a mesh emitter with collision and a heat dynamic parameter. The seal is a decal plus a camera-facing material driven by a single fill scalar.
notes: Tell: a gold assessment seal forms over the target and a wedge sweeps exactly one third of it, so the game rule reads before anything moves.
Impact: the seal slams shut, a split white and black crescent holds for two frames, and the target lurches toward the caster.
The soul is two camera-facing ribbons on one bezier path, wound around each other as a helix: one additive and pale, one alpha and black, so it is literally half holy and half dark.
Residue: sixteen instanced coins spill out white-hot, tumble, bounce and cool to tarnished gold on the floor, a one-third brand smokes under the target and the caster keeps a fading warm rim.

name: Twilight Gaze
src: All enemies lose dark and holy resistance for several turns.
blurb: A seam splits the air above the field and opens on a wet eye with a gold and obsidian iris; its gaze throws half the room into dusk gold and half into cold shadow, and the warding rings around each enemy crack and rain down as gilt and black glass.
port: Eyeball as a mesh with an iris material driven by a gaze vector and a lid mask from a screen-aligned SDF. The split lighting is two dynamic lights, one with negative intensity or a light function; shards are a Niagara mesh emitter with collision.
notes: The eye is a lit sphere alpha-clipped to an almond aperture computed in camera space, so lids open as a rift in the air while the ball keeps real specular and depth.
The iris is split down the middle: one half brushed gold metal, the other black obsidian, with a hot seam between them and a vertical slit pupil that scans the field.
Light does the enchantment: a warm gold point light on one side and a negative light sink on the other draw a twilight terminator across actors and floor, mirrored by a decal line.
Residue: each enemy loses a two-tone ward ring that shatters into instanced gold and black shards which land and glint, and ash and gold motes keep falling in the dusk.

name: Soul Wind
src: A wide line of wind deals dark damage (holy to undead/demons) and summons a spirit from each living unit hit.
blurb: The caster draws breath from the room and releases it as a broad pale gale that scours the floor and drags a translucent copy out of each body it crosses, head first, leaving the spirits hovering in the wake.
port: A Niagara system with a moving front parameter driving spawn of streak sprites and swept dust; the spirits are a duplicated skeletal mesh with a world-position-offset tear driven by a single curve and a translucent fresnel material.
notes: Tell: dust and vapour spiral into the raised hand while the room light dims toward it.
The gale is a front moving at a fixed speed; streak particles, translucent wind sheets and swept floor dust all key off when the front passes their x position.
Each spirit is an instanced mannequin shell whose vertices are offset with a height-dependent lag, so the head tears loose first and the legs stretch out of the body like vapour.
Residue: the floor keeps pale scour lines along the wind direction and the two spirits stay on, breathing faint cold light onto their former bodies.

name: Choir of Angels
src: Summons angelic singers whose song heals allies and damages undead, demons and dark units.
blurb: Three shafts of daylight open in the crypt and three small marble choristers sink down through them with folded wings; their halos ignite, the wings open, and as they sing, rings of gold sound roll out and shed feathers that drift to the floor.
port: Three skinned angel meshes with a wing blend-shape for the spread, a halo emissive parameter and a Niagara ring emitter on a beat; feathers are a mesh emitter with sway and collision.
notes: The singers are one solid raymarched layer: a tapered robe, shoulders, praying arms and a bowed head blended with smooth-min, bounded per figure for cost and shaded as pale veined marble with gilt hems.
Wings are 66 instanced feather meshes, primaries and coverts, fanned from each shoulder; a single spread value takes them from folded to open on the halo beat.
Impact is the halo ignition: a hard gold ring flashes on each figure for two frames and the shafts collapse into warm pools on the floor.
The song reads as thin camera-facing gold rings expanding on a beat from each mouth; residue is feathers that sway down and settle, plus lit dust in the light.

name: Holy Armor
src: Buff: gain large resistance to physical, fire, lightning and dark damage.
blurb: Molten gold runs up the body in the seams of an unseen harness, then floods outward into overlapping lames of translucent amber light that set like cast glass, dripping beads of gold that cool on the floor.
port: A character overlay material with a seam mask texture and two scalars (seam reveal height, plate fill), a Niagara mesh emitter for droplets with collision, and a decal for the scorch ring.
notes: Tell: a lame pattern in object space (horizontal bands on the torso and legs, rings on the arms and a centre ridge) glows as molten seams climbing from the feet.
Impact: the plates fill from the seams outward in one beat, a hard ring flashes on the floor for two frames and the light spikes.

The armour is a shell pushed off the body along normals: amber glass with gold metal reflection, a fresnel rim, a small refraction offset and bright seams, over a custom body that keeps the stage mannequin material.
Residue: drops fall from the seams on ballistic paths and land as instanced gold beads that cool from white to metal, inside a pale scorched ring.

name: Word of Chaos
src: Teleports and stuns all enemies and deals heavy fire, lightning or physical damage by type.
blurb: The caster speaks a word that tears a molten seam in the air; when it snaps shut every enemy is ripped out of place along a stream of sparks and dropped somewhere else, where one burns, one is struck by lightning and one is battered by flying flagstones.
port: Niagara: one system with a ribbon emitter per enemy for the teleport arc, an event that relocates the pawns, and three damage sub-emitters chosen by a random int. The tear is a camera-facing card with an SDF crack mask; armour residue is a material layer on the character.
notes: Tell: a jagged tear opens in front of the caster while cracks crawl outward under each enemy and their armour trembles.
Impact: the tear snaps shut behind a two-frame spiked flash, the enemies dissolve into ember shells and stream along arcs to new spots, hidden for a fifth of a second in between.
Each landing gets a different damage type so the chaos reads: lit flames and smoke, a hair-thin bolt in three strikes, and instanced flagstones with lit dust.
Residue: cooling crack rings where they stood, a scorch, a branching burn and a crushed ring where they landed, char and dust on the armour, and a dazed sway.

name: Ironize
src: All allies gain physical, fire and lightning resistance and become metallic.
blurb: Iron filings crawl across the floor from the caster to each ally, then a white-hot forging seam climbs every body from boots to helm, leaving riveted iron plate that glows, cools to dark steel and steams.
port: A character material layer with a world height mask driven by one scalar per pawn, blending to a tileable riveted iron material with an emissive temperature curve. Niagara handles filings (spline-follow), seam sparks (skeletal mesh surface sampling above the mask height) and steam.
notes: Tell: dark filings stream along curved field lines on the floor and gather at each ally boots, drawn as lit metallic specks.
The iron shell is an opaque copy of each mannequin, alpha clipped above a noisy seam line that rises over one second; the plate pattern, rivets and hammered normals are procedural in object space.
The seam front is a thin blackbody band that throws stretched sparks and slag drips, and its light rides up the body so the floor and neighbours change colour.
Residue: plates cool from orange to grey iron over three seconds, steam lifts off the shoulders, and slag splashes harden on the floor around the feet. A hard glint pops on each helm as it completes.

name: Flesh Fiend
src: Summons a huge regenerating fleshy mass with a melee attack.
blurb: A rope of the caster’s blood feeds a boiling pool that heaves up into a ton of raw, breathing meat, which winds back a fleshy club and smashes the enemy, its torn skin knitting shut behind it.
port: A skeletal mesh with blendshape breathing and a wet subsurface material; regeneration is a wound mask animated toward zero. Spawn from a pool decal with a rise animation, and drive the attack with an authored montage plus Niagara gore and dust on the hit notify.
notes: Tell: a ballistic stream of blood leaves the caster’s hand and fills a pool that boils with worley bubbles.
The fiend is a solid raymarched SDF that writes depth: smooth-min lobes that pulse out of phase, a horizontal maw with teeth, bone spurs, and a pseudopod built from capsules along a moving bezier.
Flesh shading layers pale fat, dark veins and wet specular over a deep red base, with a fake subsurface term from the effect lights so the mass glows where it is thin.
Impact: the club lands on the enemy with a pale crescent, blood spray and floor dust; afterwards torn grooves on the mass close up and steam, and gore chunks and the pool stay behind.

name: Permanence
src: Buff: your buffs, debuffs and temporary summons last longer.
blurb: Gold sand pours off the caster like time running out, until two engraved bronze rings rise and lock around them with a clang; the falling sand stops dead in the air and begins to drift back up.
port: Niagara: grains with a per-particle time-scale curve driven by a user parameter (1 before the lock, 0 during the hold, negative after). Rings are static meshes with an engraved metal material on a timeline; the floor mark is a decal with an emissive cool-down.
notes: Tell: grains spawn on the body surface and fall under gravity, piling at the feet, while two bronze rings climb out of the floor spinning fast.
Impact: the rings slam to a stop at chest height, crossing like an armillary; a hard ring flash and a pale light spike mark the lock.
Every grain is closed-form: its falling position is frozen at the lock time, held, then eased onto a slow upward spiral, so time visibly stops and reverses.
Residue: a clock-face circle with twelve ticks is cut into the floor and filled with molten gold that cools to metal, and the sand pile stays.

name: Seraph Wings
blurb: A pair of energy wings behind the shoulders with layered feather rows, a slow flap, a white-hot leading edge and falling feather motes.
port: Unreal: two skinned or WPO-animated cards with the feather mask baked to a texture and the flap in World Position Offset. Motes are a Niagara emitter sampling the wing mesh surface.
notes: Each wing is one subdivided plane. The vertex shader fans it out from an arm curve, so uv.x runs root to tip and uv.y runs from the feather tips to the arm.
Feathers are three overlapping rows drawn in the fragment shader: a rounded tip profile per feather, a dark seam, a shaft line and a bright rim where each row ends.
The flap is a fold angle driven by a sine that lags toward the tip, so the wing rolls through the beat instead of hinging like a door.
The Flame parameter erodes the feather tips with scrolling noise and adds heat toward the edge, which turns the same mesh into phoenix or demon wings.
Feather motes are particles born on the wing surface using the same shape function, so they always fall from where the wing actually is.

name: Weapon Enchant
blurb: A floating blade with glowing runes and edges, an elemental shell, a camera-facing aura, two orbiting ribbons and sparks or drips.
port: Unreal: weapon material layer for runes and edge glow, a shell mesh with World Position Offset, and a Niagara system attached to weapon sockets for the aura ribbon and sparks. Expose element colour and flow direction as user parameters.
notes: The sword is lit and opaque. Runes from rune() sit on the ridge and the cutting edges glow, both fed by noise that scrolls from guard to tip.
The shell is a second copy of the blade scaled outward in the vertex shader and eroded with fast noise, so the element hugs the steel.
The big silhouette comes from a strip billboarded around the blade axis. It never shows an edge and carries the flames, mist or lightning arcs.
Flow sets whether the element rises like fire or sinks like frost, and the same value drives the particles into embers or drips.
Two ribbons follow a closed-form helix around the blade, so the trail needs no history buffer.

name: Spark
src: Launches a spray of unpredictable sparks that travel over the ground in random directions, bouncing off walls, until they hit an enemy or expire. Reference: research/refs/poe_spark_wiki.png.
blurb: A flick of the hand throws a spray of crackling lightning knots that drop to the floor and wander off on their own random walks, dragging thin tendrils over the flagstones and spitting white sparks, ricocheting off the edge of the arena until two of them find the target and the rest sputter out.
port: Niagara: one emitter of 4 to 8 knot particles with a random-walk velocity module and plane collision, each spawning a short beam emitter set (3 to 5 beams between random points inside a 1 m sphere, reseeded per tick) plus 1 to 3 ground ribbons sampling the particle position history. Scorch flicks are decals on the death event.
notes: Matches the PoE read: each projectile is a compact knot about a metre across made of 3 to 5 short jagged arcs inside a sphere, reseeded every 1 or 2 frames, with a soft white core, not a continuous arc from the caster.

The walk is an integrated noisy heading baked at load and parameterised by arc length, so the speed and duration params scale the traversal; knots ricochet off an invisible 5 m stage circle and off the caster, and a knot that touches the target is absorbed there.
Each knot drags 1 to 3 thin tendrils over the floor behind it (midpoint displacement bolts along its own path history, coarse levels reseeding slowly), and sheds tiny velocity-stretched white sparks.
Every knot carries its own point light so the flagstones flicker under it; a fizzle leaves a small Lichtenberg scorch flick and a wisp of lit smoke, a hit pops with arcs over the body.

name: Shock Nova
src: Casts a ring of lightning around the caster: an inner ring of glowing runes and a larger outer ring of lightning that shocks everything on its edge. Reference: research/refs/poe_shock_nova_wiki.png.
blurb: The caster slams the charge into the stone and a ring of burning orange-white runes ignites around them between two thin blue-white circles; a beat later a thin outer ring of white-violet lightning races out to four metres, throwing short arcs in and out from its edge, and dies back while the runes burn down last.
port: Niagara: a ring emitter on a radius curve spawning beam emitters along the rim (circumferential) and a second set of short radial beams with random sign, a rune-band decal material with a polar glyph atlas driven by an ignite sweep and a burn curve, and a core light. The slam is a montage notify.
notes: Matches the PoE read: the energy lives in two ring bands, a rune band at 2 m (runeRing glyph script between two thin circles, warm orange-white against the blue-white bolts) and a thin lightning ring at 4 m; the floor inside is left dark.

The outer ring is circumferential midpoint displacement bolts overlapping around the rim plus short in-and-out arcs that leave the rim only, all reseeding every 1 or 2 frames; its radius is an ease-out curve with an analytic inverse so sparks, haze and the shock on each target fire as the rim passes.
The rune band ignites in a quick sweep on the release frame with a bloom, flickers per glyph while it burns, and fades last; a faint ash glyph decal is left under it.
A bright core at the caster (chest glow, hand static before the slam) and eight lights: core, three on the outer rim, two warm on the rune band and one per shocked target.

name: Frost Nova
sub: Diablo II / Path of Exile archetype
src: The caster releases a ring of freezing cold that expands across the floor, chilling and freezing everything it passes.
blurb: Cold is drawn into the hands and slammed into the floor; a crisp ring of jagged ice erupts and collapses outward, leaving feathered frost and rimed foes behind.
port: Niagara: one emitter-level float (front radius from a curve) drives a mesh emitter of ice shards spawned on a disc with spawn delay from distance, plus a ribbon-free mist emitter. Frost is a deferred decal whose material reads the same radius from a parameter collection; the fern pattern is a material function with a 3x3 cell search. Rime is a character overlay material driven by the same radius.
notes: Read: a crisp ring of ice racing over the floor, less than a second from slam to full radius. One analytic front radius (ease-out) drives every element, so shards, frost, mist, lights and rime all agree on where the cold is.

The wave is 600 instanced 5-sided crystal meshes placed on an R2 low-discrepancy sequence. Each erupts with an overshoot when the front reaches it, holds a few frames and sinks while it shatters into lit chips; one in ten stays as a stub. Vertex jitter is hashed by position so the jagged faces stay closed. Material is the shared iceMat with a base-to-tip value ramp.

Floor frost is fern-frost dendrites: veins aimed outward from the centre with barbs at 60 degrees (ice grows on hexagonal axes), one frond per jittered cell at two scales, over a hex-tiled (Mikkelsen) noise haze, so the 9 m decal never repeats.

Anticipation gathers motes and rime at both rigged hands while vapour is pulled in along the floor. Freezing mist is carried by the front and puffs off each collapsing shard, lit by three lights riding the ring.
Foes are rimed from the feet up on the side facing the blast, and a crust of crystals grows at their feet. Light goes first, then mist, then shards; the frost and stubs sublimate last.

name: Frozen Orb
src: Launches a slow, glowing orb of ice that sheds a spiral of ice bolts in every direction as it flies, then bursts into a final nova of bolts.
blurb: A bright blue-white sphere of ice drifts slowly from the hand at chest height, shedding slim pointed bolts in two turning spiral arms along its whole path, then bursts into a ring of bolts and a floor flash.
port: Niagara: the orb is a projectile emitter whose spawn-rate event fires bolt meshes with an angle from Emitter.Age times a spin rate; bolts are constant-velocity mesh particles with a ribbon child, and a collision event spawns chips and a decal. The final burst is a death event spawning a ring of the same bolt emitter plus a decal.
notes: Reference: research/refs/d2_frozen_orb_wiki.png and d2r_frozen_orb_video.png. Read: a glowing 0.6 m sphere crawling 6.4 m in 1.85 s (3.5 m/s) at 1 m height; dozens of thin pointed blue-white bolts with a short white trail laid out in a spiral around the whole path; a 24-bolt nova and a bright floor flash at the end of its range.

The orb is a fresnel-lit sphere on the shared iceMat with a hot blue-white core, 18 short crystal spikes that turn with the emission angle, a rayed halo, glitter dust and a sinking vapour trail. One light rides the orb, a second lights the floor beneath it.

Bolts are straight (no gravity): each leaves the orb surface at 5.6 to 6.4 m/s on a shallow descent and strikes the floor 2.6 to 4.2 m out. Two arms turn at 1.1 rev/s and release 96 bolts over the flight, so successive bolts step 14 degrees and lay out two clean spiral arms. Each bolt is one closed-form line (birth, start, velocity, floor time) evaluated by the lathe icicle mesh, a short camera-facing trail, a frost splash decal at the hit and lit chips that shatter off it.

The nova throws 24 bolts in an even ring, holds a 3-frame star and a 4-frame floor flash, grows a fern-frost decal at the burst point and breaks the spikes off to tumble and bounce. Light goes first, then mist, then chips; splashes and the burst frost sublimate last.

name: Arctic Armour
src: A self buff that raises a crystalline barrier of frost around the caster: blows that land on it are blunted and shatter ice outward, and the ground inside it is chilled.
blurb: Frost gathers in both hands, then a translucent, swirling shell of frost closes around the caster at hip height, dozens of small icicle shards drift inside and on it catching glints, a ring of frost crystals rims its base, a hit flings large pale icicles outward and the shell closes again, and at the end the shell thins, the shards fall and melt and the floor frost fades last.
notes: Reference: PoE2 Arctic Armour (research/refs/poe2_arctic_armour_idle_video.png, _video2.png, _burst_video.png). Read: a ~1.3 m translucent frost sphere around the character, swirling, pale blue-white, glinting; small shards inside and on it; a frost ring on the floor; body only gets a cold sheen; the hit flings large pale icicles.

Shell: a sphere mesh (1.3 x 1.25 x 1.3 m, centred 0.9 m up) in two passes (far hemisphere then near hemisphere, culled). Its frost is the hex-tiled noise sheet sampled triplanar (triH, so no uv seam) under a two-phase flow map that rotates differentially around the vertical axis plus a simplex warp, so the frost visibly swirls without stretching or repeating. Alpha is fresnel-weighted (rim 6x the face) so the body stays readable; crystalline veins in the crack channel are shaded with iceMat and env reflections; the frost refracts the scene slightly.

Shards: 240 instanced five-sided faceted prisms (4 to 11 cm) drifting on spherical paths, 70 percent on the shell surface and 30 percent inside, tumbling slowly, each appearing on one of four density steps (0.55 s apart). A glint plane sweeps through the shell every 3.6 s lighting the facets it crosses, and single facets twinkle from iceMat sparkle and the key reflection.

Hit: at the impact marker 40 large pale rimed icicles (16 to 34 cm) are flung outward ballistically from the caster, tumble, land tip first and melt; the shell loses 60 percent of its density and re-densifies over a second.

Floor: a hex-tiled frost decal with a brighter lip at the shell base ring, and 90 instanced ring crystals; both thaw to a wet sheen that fades last. Body: a thin rimed fresnel sheen on the stage mannequin only, no crystals on the body. Cold vapour is born on the shell and sinks along it to the floor; diamond dust swirls inside with the shell flow.

name: Geyser
src: Slams the ground to burst a pressurised column of water up out of the floor, hurling enemies caught above it and drenching the area around it.
blurb: The caster slams the floor, a wet crack races to the target, the ground heaves and splits, and a seven metre column of white water roars up, shedding sheets and ropes that rain back into a churning, puddled splash zone.
port: Niagara: two mesh cylinders with a panning two-phase flow material (hex-tiling node in UE5.4+ or a custom HLSL tile breaker) and refraction; ribbon emitters spawning along the column with gravity and drag; GPU sprites for spray with velocity alignment and collision to spawn ripple decals; a puddle decal with a ripple flipbook normal.
notes: Read: a vertical white column three to four times the caster height, held for under two seconds, raining back. Slam, heave, roar, patter.

The column is two displaced tubes (dense core, torn outer sheath) shaded with two-phase flow-mapped, stochastic hex-tiled noise (triH) scrolling upward, so the 7 m surface never repeats; foam versus clear water is decided by the flow noise and the view angle, and the clear water writes refraction.

Sheets and ropes are instanced ribbons whose every row is a parcel of water emitted from the column at a different time and flown ballistically with drag, so they peel off, sag under gravity and erode into droplets as they age.
Spray is velocity-stretched lit droplets (an eruption burst, then sustained shedding); foam and mist are lit puffs (puffLit) and two thin crown splashes ring out on the eruption and on the fall-back.
Ground: floor plates heave and are thrown and bounce; the decal carries the travelling crack from the slam, a wet zone with mirror puddles and procedural rain ripples that fades last.

name: Blessed Hammer
src: Each cast conjures a spectral warhammer that spirals outward around the caster, tumbling end over end and ringing off every foe it passes through.
blurb: Three quick casts throw three engraved spectral warhammers that tumble end over end along overlapping clockwise spirals, ring off the foes they pierce and dissolve into motes.
port: Niagara: one emitter per cast spawning a mesh particle whose position is a spiral curve sampled by normalised age, with a ribbon emitter attached for the trail and a second for the spin smear. Collision with pawns fires an event emitter for the glint and spark burst; the hammer material uses an engraving mask with emissive in the grooves and a dissolve driven by particle age.
notes: Hammers are lit meshes, not sprites: a rounded, flared box head and a lathed haft per instance, shaded as polished metal with engraved grooves that hold the holy glow.

The path is an Archimedean spiral (three turns, 0.55 to 2.9 m) with a speed profile halfway between constant angular and constant linear speed, so the hammers whirl near the caster and sweep wide at the edge.

Each cast aims the hand at a slightly different heading, so the three spirals cross instead of stacking. Hit times are solved in JS from the same path and baked into GLSL arrays; flashes, sparks, flinches and lights read them.
Two ribbon sets: a wide soft trail on the centre path textured in path time so streaks stay put in the world, and thin smears on the pommel and face that draw the tumble loops.

Impact is a hard four point glint and ring for three frames, then thin ringing circles, velocity stretched sparks that bounce and cool on the floor, and a light spike. Motes shed along the path are the residue.

name: Righteous Fire
src: A sustained self-immolation aura: the caster burns, a magic circle ignites under their feet and a ring of fire marks the edge of the area that burns every enemy inside it.
blurb: Fire kindles in both palms, a glyph circle with a violet pentagram draws itself under the caster and a thin orange ring races out to the edge of the aura; the three burn steadily, then the ring gutters, the glyph goes last and a scorch ring remains.
port: Niagara: two decal materials (ring and magic circle) driven by a front radius and a draw parameter, with the circle built from SDF rings, a star polyline and a rune atlas; a torus-shaped emitter for ring flames and embers; a skeletal-socket emitter on both hands and forearms for body flames; a refraction ring mesh for the shimmer. Sustained phase is a looping state with staggered fade curves per element.
notes: Built against the Path of Exile wiki screenshot: three elements and almost nothing in between. The outer ring is one ground decal, a thin band on the front radius with a doubled inner line, a feathered flame fringe scrolling outward and a soft halo, so it reads as a drawn circle at gameplay distance.

The magic circle is procedural: two orange fire rings and a rune ring (library rune and runeRing) that rotate slowly one way, a violet pentagram and two thin violet circles that rotate the other way. Rings draw by an angular sweep and the pentagram line by line at release.

Low licking flames and embers are soft particles born on the ring and on the glyph edge; a tube of noise-driven refraction above the outer ring is the heat shimmer. Fire on the caster uses the hand uniforms and handAt, with short forearm, shoulder and head licks and a hot white core sprite on each palm; the channel pose gets an at point so the right hand is raised to the side and the two hot points stay apart, as in the reference.

Eight lights: the glyph centre, four on the ring, both hands and one rim light placed opposite the camera so the body carries a red-orange rim. Fall-off is staggered: ring first, then hands, glyph last, and a soot ring with a pale ash lip and cooling embers stays on the floor.
Ground noise is hex-tiled (nzH); polar lookups use nzL with integer repeats so the rings have no seam. Hold motion runs on absolute time so the sustained phase loops.

name: Fireball Volley
sub: Path of Exile archetype (multiple projectiles), Diablo multishot lineage
src: One cast throws a shotgun fan of fireballs that detonate on everything in front of the caster.
blurb: A single throw splits a ball of fire into seven, fanning out like buckshot; they burst on three mannequins and the floor in a rippling wall of explosions that leaves soot, embers and scorch marks.
port: Niagara: one emitter spawns N projectile particles in a cone with per-particle speed and delay, each with a ribbon and a collision event that triggers burst emitters and a deferred decal. In VFX Graph, a GPU event per collision drives the burst systems.
notes: The read is one gesture, many projectiles: one fire mass gathers in the hand and splits on the release frame into seven balls with their own launch jitter, speed and arc, so the impacts ripple instead of landing together.
Each ball is a displaced sphere with a fire-to-soot trail; the explosions are alpha puffs whose hot core cools into soot lit by the impact lights (no additive stacking to white).
Impact frames are small spiked bursts held three frames. The scale is carried by up to eight point lights that are sorted by intensity every frame.
Ground interaction: hex-tiled scorch decals with pale ash lips and cooling cracks, kicked pebbles with gravity and bounce, embers that skid on the stone, and mannequins that flinch from the hits.

name: Meteor
src: Calls a burning rock down from the sky onto a marked spot after a short delay, leaving the ground on fire.
blurb: A raised arm marks the ground with a glyph and a growing shadow; a burning rock streaks down at a steep angle, detonates, flings molten debris and leaves a cracked crater of burning ground that slowly cools.
port: Sequencer or timeline: a decal plus a ground-projected material for the glyph and shadow, a falling mesh with a ribbon emitter, then a collision event that spawns the burst emitters, a mesh-particle debris emitter with collision, and a deferred crater decal whose heat parameter is driven by a curve.
notes: The read is a telegraph then a payoff: the glyph and a darkening shadow show where it will land, and the meteor light reaches the floor before the rock enters the frame.
The rock is a lit mesh with an ablating white-hot leading face and glowing fissures, wrapped in a camera-facing flame ribbon and a fire-to-soot particle trail that stays hanging in the air.

Impact: a spiked graphic burst for three frames, alpha explosion puffs that cool into lit soot, a shock ring, and instanced molten chunks with gravity and one bounce that keep glowing where they land.
Residue: a hex-tiled crater decal with a shaded rim, radial ejecta streaks and molten cracks that cool from white to red to black, with flames licking over it while the heat lasts.

name: Grasping Vines
sub: Path of Exile archetype (Grasping Vines debuff)
src: A tether debuff: each stack is a thick elastic vine running from the victim to a root knot on the floor. The vines stretch as the victim moves and twang back when a stack breaks.
blurb: The caster gathers sap light and sends it into the floor; root lines race to the victim and eight stiff cable vines snap up one after another from knots in the ground to latch on hips and thighs. The victim lunges, the vines stretch, thin and brighten, two snap and whip back to their anchors, the rest hold, then all wither grey and sink into the floor.
notes: Reference: research/refs/poe_grasping_vines_wiki.png (poewiki Grasping Vines). The read is a fan of 6 to 10 thick, stiff, cable-like vines from the hips and thighs to anchor knots 1 to 2.5 m away, dark teal bark, pale thorn studs, yellow-green sap glow along the length and brightest at the tips and anchors, a faint green floor glow at each knot. Nothing climbs or coils around the body.

Each vine is an instanced tube whose vertices slide along a cubic bezier rod from its anchor to its latch point (a slight upward bow that sways). The rod is rebuilt every frame from the victim transform, so when the victim lunges the vines stretch, the radius thins by the length ratio and the sap brightens. A snapped vine recoils toward its knot with a damped twang, whips its loose end up and drops it on the floor.

Anchors sit on a golden-angle fan around the victim, so the count parameter removes vines from the end of the list without leaving gaps. Latch points are solved on the surface of the nearer thigh or the belt facing the anchor, in mannequin space, and follow the actor lean (the actor and the shaders share one transform function).

Bark is stochastic hex-tiled noise in (around, metres along) space with three twisted ridges; the sap is a flow-mapped noise stripe in the grooves, gated by stretch and life. Thorn studs are instanced lathe cones on the same curve parameter with pale tips. Knots are lathe meshes displaced by triplanar hex noise with three short root fingers each; the floor decal is one hex-tiled layer with the racing root lines, the underground spread lines and a soft glow disc per anchor.

Timing: cast with a gather at the hands, release into the floor, root lines at 7.5 m per second, vines every 85 ms (impact marker on the first latch), a sway hold, a struggle with two snaps and a haul-back, then wither (grey, roughen, sag), retract tip first into the knots, and the anchor glow fades last.

name: Tornado
sub: Path of Exile / Diablo IV druid archetype
src: The druid flings a whirlwind ahead; it wanders across the ground as a towering funnel, battering enemies and hauling dust, leaves and stones around itself.
blurb: A gust leaves the hands and spins up into a tall, leaning funnel that meanders across the floor, dragging a dense dust skirt, rings of stones and leaves, scouring a pale trail, shoving a bystander aside, and finally unravelling and dropping everything it carried.
port: Niagara: a spline-driven system whose base follows a wandering path. Three funnel meshes with panning 3D noise (or a heterogeneous volume), mesh-renderer debris with a vortex force and a kill-to-ballistic event, sprite skirt and inflow emitters, and a decal trail written into a render target.
notes: The funnel is three nested shells, each drawn back faces then front faces, with its own rotation speed and twist. Their streaks are ridged 3D simplex noise sampled on a rotating circle, so they never tile or seam.

Opacity grows with the shell thickness seen along the view (one over N dot V), which turns thin shells into a volume with dense silhouettes; dust is lit by the key light, ambient and the effect light.
Stones and leaves lie on the floor until the funnel reaches them, then are lifted onto orbits at three radii with Kepler-like speeds; on collapse they leave on their tangents, fall and bounce once.
A dense skirt of lit puffs and an inflow of grit spiral into the foot. The floor gets a stochastic hex-tiled scour along the travelled path and a spiral dust ring under the current base.
Release on the throw, impact when the funnel reaches the bystander, a long fall-off as the walls erode, and the trail and dropped debris as residue.

name: Blade Vortex
src: Each cast adds another ethereal blade to the storm orbiting the caster; the blades cut everything they pass and expire one by one.
blurb: Twelve pale green-cyan sabres stream from the casting hand and settle on three orbit rings around the caster, each drawing a thin circling trail, while a green-grey mist whirls at the centre; they expire one at a time in the order they were cast.
port: Niagara: one mesh emitter with a ring module (angle = slot + speed[ring]*age, radius[ring]) spawning one blade per stack event, a ribbon renderer sampling the same orbit, a sprite emitter for the lit mist with a vortex force. Blade material: translucent with fresnel edge emissive and an erosion scalar; trails as additive ribbons with age fade.
notes: Reference: the Blade Vortex wiki screenshot (research/refs/poe_blade_vortex_wiki.png): curved sabre silhouettes on two or three radii, flat to their orbit, thin ring trails, a mist vortex at the centre.

The sabre is a custom lens-section mesh (curved centre line, widening belly, tapered tip, short hilt) registered as a GEO builder and drawn instanced. Each instance is placed in the vertex shader on an analytic orbit: three radii at three angular speeds, slot angles spread per ring, with radius wobble, height weave and a slow roll so no ring is a rigid wheel.

The ghost material is two passes: an alpha body (tint plus env() reflection scaled by fresnel, streak noise) and an additive shell (hot cutting edge, dimmer spine, fresnel rim, simplex flicker) plus a faint billboard halo per blade. Blades materialise and expire by soft alpha erosion of 3D simplex noise with a glowing rim, shedding motes.

Trails are camera-facing ribbons that resample the orbit function over nearly one full turn into the past, so every blade draws its own thin circle; the ribbon holds and fades after its blade expires, so the rings are the residue that goes last.

The centre vortex is lit vapour sprites (puffLit under the effect lights, green-grey albedo, a touch of tint) spiralling in with the stack count, plus thin additive wisps and five tumbling blade ghosts inside it. Four quick rig casts keep the hand out while the blades stack from it.

name: Corpse Explosion
src: The necromancer points at a corpse; it detonates in a flash of fire and hurls gore over a wide radius, damaging everything it lands on.
blurb: A quick point drops a curse on a fallen body; it swells for a breath, then rips apart in a yellow-white fire flash as a hundred wet red chunks fan out over four metres, bounce, and settle in splatter that stays while the smoke lifts off the corpse.
notes: Reference: the Corpse Explosion wiki screenshot (research/refs/d2_corpse_explosion_wiki.png): one hot yellow-white fire puff at the corpse and a wide spray of 50+ small red chunks spread over a large radius, landing and staying as red splatter; blood, not pink mist.

The corpse is the stage mannequin laid on its back in the vertex shader. It swells under the skin for .14 s, then tears: each vertex is assigned a jittered 3D cell, cells fly ballistically as rigid pieces and triangles that straddle two cells are discarded in the fragment shader (fwidth of the cell id), so the shell rips along ragged seams and turns to wet flesh inside.

Gore is one instanced rock mesh in three size classes (chips, lumps, hunks) with a deterministic per-chunk launch: range drawn from the spray radius, speed solved for that range, one bounce with restitution, a short slide, then rest. Material: wet dark-red albedo with a low-roughness specular, dark creases, and bone-white ends on a quarter of the larger pieces.

Blood: velocity-stretched lit streak sprites trail the larger chunks, a droplet spray follows the same fan, and splatter decals are instanced ground quads placed at the first contact point of each chunk, elongated along its travel and shaped with hex-tiled noise (nzH) so no two splats repeat. A hex-tiled pool, radial streaks and droplets sit under the corpse.

Fire: a 3-frame yellow-white flash quad (soft puff edge with a few short spikes, under the blast size), a blackbody fireball of alpha-blended puffs that cool into lit soot within half a second, a smoke column that starts after the fire and rises for three seconds, and embers with gravity of which twenty lie glowing on the floor. The flash light is near-white and short; an ember-orange light lingers on the chunks and smoke. Residue order: light, flash, fire, most embers, smoke, then the floor embers and the splats fade last. The smoke layer is drawn before the fireball so the dark soot never masks the hot core. Fire tint: warm tints use the untinted blackbody ramp, green or blue tints switch to the tinted flame ramp (Poison flash variant).

name: Cut Gemstone
blurb: A faceted gem turning above a pedestal, with real internal bounces, colour fringing and facet glints.
port: Unreal: a translucent or opaque material with a custom node that runs the plane loop in local space and samples a cubemap. In Unity use a Shader Graph custom function. Glints are a Niagara emitter sampling the static mesh vertices.
notes: The gem is a convex solid, so the shader intersects the view ray with its 25 facet planes analytically and bounces it inside up to four times.
Each exit is refracted three times with slightly different indices, one per colour channel. That is the dispersion fire you see on the diamond.
Light that never escapes is kept as a deep tinted body colour, which gives the stone its saturated dark facets next to bright ones.
Reflections sample a small procedural studio environment with hard softboxes, because a gem needs contrast to sparkle.
Glint sprites sit on real facet corners and flash at random, so the sparkle is tied to the geometry.

name: Potion Flask
blurb: A corked glass flask with a sloshing, softly glowing liquid, rising bubbles and thick glass reflections.
port: Unreal: liquid as a masked material with a world-aligned plane clip and two-sided shading that swaps the normal on back faces. Glass as a separate translucent mesh with a reflection capture. Bubbles in Niagara, killed at the fill height.
notes: The liquid is a slightly smaller copy of the flask, alpha clipped at a tilting plane. Back faces seen through the cut are shaded as the flat liquid surface.
Liquid depth is faked by stepping a refracted ray through 3D noise in object space, so the swirl shifts with parallax like a volume.
Glass is two alpha passes, back faces then front faces. Opacity and reflection both follow fresnel, so the silhouette is thick and the centre is clear.
Bubbles follow the flask profile and stop at the fill line. They skip the depth test because they live inside the opaque liquid.
A point light inside the flask tints the floor, which grounds the glow.

name: Holographic Item Card
blurb: A rare item card floating upright with a holographic foil frame, an embossed rune and a sweeping sheen. Move the pointer to tilt it.
port: UMG or UI Toolkit material for inventory tooltips, or a mesh card in world space. Feed the tilt from cursor position or a gyroscope. The foil needs only the camera vector in tangent space plus one noise texture.
notes: Foil colour is a cosine palette indexed by the view vector in card tangent space, so the rainbow slides as the card tilts.
A voronoi layer gives each foil flake its own grating direction. Flakes flash at different angles, which is what sells real holo print.
Frame and rune are one height field. It bends the normal for lighting and also offsets the foil lookup, so bevels pick up different hues.
The art window uses the same tangent view vector as a parallax offset, which puts the nebula behind the card surface.
Pointer position drives the tilt in the vertex shader. A slow idle sway keeps it alive when nobody touches it.

name: Runestone
blurb: A standing stone with a carved rune whose grooves pulse with light, shedding sparks and colouring the floor.
port: Unreal: a mesh decal or a second UV channel carries the rune SDF texture. Use it for normal, AO and emissive in one material and drive the pulse with a panner along V. Sparks spawn from the mesh surface filtered by the emissive mask.
notes: The glyph is the rune() SDF projected through the slab along its depth axis, so both faces are carved from one function.
The same distance field does three jobs: it darkens the groove, bends the normal at the groove walls and drives the emissive core.
The pulse travels up the strokes instead of blinking, and a wide falloff of the SDF fakes light spilling onto the stone next to the cut.
Stone is flat shaded with per-facet value variation, crack lines and moss on upward faces, so it stays stone under coloured light.
Two point lights sit just off each face. They are what actually colours the floor.

name: Crystal Cluster
blurb: A cluster of faceted crystals growing from rock, with glowing cores, inner fracture veils and hard reflections.
port: Unreal: one material instance per cluster using a refraction vector into a cubemap plus a BumpOffset style lookup into a volume or tiling noise texture. Use per-instance random for the seed and instance the crystals with a foliage or PCG tool.
notes: Each crystal refracts the view ray in object space and steps it through 3D noise. Thin ridges of that noise become fracture veils that slide with parallax.
The refracted ray is also bounced off a fake back facet and looked up in the environment, which gives the hard light and dark flips of real crystal.
Glow is strongest along the axis and at the root, so the light has a source and the tips stay clear and dark.
Normals come from screen derivatives, so every facet is perfectly flat and catches its own reflection.
One shader serves all five crystals. Only the transform and a seed change.

name: Skill Bar Slots
blurb: Four action bar slots showing idle, cooling down, ready flash and proc states at once, with hover glow and a press ripple.
port: UMG: one material on an Image per slot with scalar parameters for Cooldown, Proc and Ready time, and the icon as a texture parameter. Drive hover and press from the button events. In UI Toolkit use a custom shader graph on a VisualElement.
notes: Each slot is one rounded box SDF. The same distance drives the icon mask, the bevelled metal frame, the socket shadow and every glow.
The cooldown is an angle test in icon space: the unfinished wedge is desaturated and darkened, and two thin lit lines mark the sweep edges.
The proc border samples noise in angle and distance space so the energy travels around the frame, with two comet heads for a clear direction.
Hover comes from u_mouse and scales the slot up slightly. A press scales it down and sends a ring out from the pointer, clipped to the icon.
The ready slot replays its flash on a loop so a still frame and a video both show it: white-out, diagonal sheen and an expanding frame echo.

name: Experience Bar
blurb: Ornate experience bar with a level badge: flowing sheen in the fill, a sparkling leading edge, tick marks and a level-up burst at full.
port: UMG: a single material with a Fill scalar. Keep ticks and frame in the same material so the bar is one draw. Trigger the level-up burst from a timeline that drives a Burst scalar instead of the loop used here.
notes: The fill is a cylinder: a vertical profile gives a lit top band and a dark underside, then two noise octaves scroll along it as a sheen.
The leading edge is where the eye should go, so it gets a hot line, a soft halo and small glints that trail behind it.
Ticks are metal slivers drawn over both trough and fill, which makes progress readable in tenths at a glance.
At Fill = 1 the badge fires a looping burst: white-out, an expanding ring, rays and the level number punching up by one.
Frame and badge use the SDF gradient as a bevel normal, lit from the top left, with noise for wear and patina.

name: Loading Sigil
blurb: Loading indicator: rune rings that write themselves in and out, a forged progress track and a core that beats in time.
port: UMG: one material with Progress as a scalar parameter fed by the streaming level load. Bake runes to a strip texture and scroll the window mask in polar UVs. In UI Toolkit drive the same shader graph from the scene load operation progress.
notes: Each ring owns an angular window with a moving head and a breathing length, like a spinner. Runes and guide circles are masked by it, so they draw on and wipe off.
The head of each window is brighter than its tail, which gives direction without any particles.
Progress lives in a channel cut into a metal bezel. The fill is an angle test with a round cap and a hot bead on the leading end.
The core beat sends a faint ring outward through the whole sigil so the layers feel connected.
At 100 percent every window opens fully and the core flares: the indicator resolves instead of just stopping.

name: Passive Tree Nodes
blurb: Eight passive nodes on a forged web: allocated links carry energy along the path, keystones get an ornate frame and the hovered node lights up.
port: UMG: nodes are widgets with one shared material (Allocated, Hover, Keystone scalars). Links are a spline or stretched image widget with a panning material whose U runs from parent to child. Batch by atlas so a 1000 node tree stays cheap.
notes: Nodes and links live in constant arrays. A Points spent parameter allocates nodes in order, so every state of the tree can be reviewed with one slider.
Link energy is a pulse train in the segment parameter, moving from the earlier node to the later one, over a slower noise shimmer.
A link with only one allocated end shows a faint marching dash: it tells the player where the next point can go.
Keystones add an eight point star plate and a second ring behind the standard socket, so importance reads from silhouette before colour.
Hover is a distance test against u_mouse. It scales the node, brightens the rim and adds a halo, the same response a controller focus would get.

name: Critical Hit Number
blurb: Damage number pop: seven-segment SDF digits slam in over a crit star burst, overshoot, float up and burn away.
port: UMG: a text block with an SDF font and a material that adds the outline, gradient and erosion (Dissolve scalar), animated by a widget animation for scale and translation. Spawn the burst as a second image or a Niagara UI particle behind it.
notes: Three beats in 1.6 s: a converging glint (anticipation), a two frame white flash with the number at 2.6 times scale (impact), then float and erosion (dissipation).
Digits are seven hex-ended segments chosen by a bitmask, so any integer up to five digits is drawn with no font texture.
The punch is easeOutBack on scale. It overshoots below final size and settles, which sells weight better than a linear shrink.
A dark outline and offset shadow keep the number readable over the burst. The burst itself is kept below bloom threshold behind the digits.
The exit is noise erosion with a hot burn line on the dissolve front, not an alpha fade.

name: Boss Health Bar
blurb: Boss health bar with a horned skull crest: viscous shimmering fill, a pale damage chunk that lags and drains after each hit, and phase gems.
port: UMG: one material with Health and GhostHealth scalars. Set Health immediately from gameplay and interpolate GhostHealth after a delay in the widget tick or with a timeline. The crest is a separate image so the bar can stretch to any width.
notes: The skull is all SDF: a cranium circle smooth-unioned with a jaw box, minus eye, nose and tooth cuts. The SDF gradient gives it a bone bevel.
Damage lag is two fill levels. Health snaps down on the hit while a pale ghost level holds for half a second and then eases down to meet it.
The demo loops a hit every four seconds and also hits on click. The bar shakes for a few frames and the ghost chunk flashes white on impact.
Quarter ticks and three phase gems under the bar show thresholds. Gems go dark as health falls past them.
Eye sockets glow in the bar colour and flare on each hit, which ties the emblem to the gameplay event.

name: Frozen Solid
blurb: The mannequin encased in ice: faceted surface, blue depth, frosted rim, twinkling glints and cold mist at the feet.
port: Overlay or swap material on the character: voronoi normal texture, Subsurface or a custom wrap term, and Fresnel into a frost mask. Blend it in by a Frozen scalar so the same material handles the freeze transition.
notes: A 3D voronoi gives every cell one tilted normal, so the smooth mesh catches light like chipped ice without any extra geometry.
Depth is faked three ways: wrapped lighting, a back-light transmission term and crack lines sampled at two parallax offsets along the view ray.
Frost is a noise mask biased to upward faces. It raises roughness and albedo, so the rim goes white while the core stays saturated.
Sparkles are hashed cells that fire only at certain view angles, so they twinkle when the camera or the light moves.
Ice shards, a frost decal and sinking mist tie the figure to the ground.

name: Target Highlight
blurb: Selected-enemy treatment: a crisp outline, a soft rim pulse, a rotating floor ring and an overhead marker, coloured by faction.
port: Outline as a post-process on custom depth or stencil for production; the inverted hull works for a quick overlay material. The ring is a decal or mesh plane with the SDF baked to a texture, and colour comes from the faction data asset.
notes: The outline is an inverted hull: the mesh pushed along its normals, showing only faces that point away from the camera, so the body covers all but the rim.
The push distance scales with camera distance, which keeps the line the same width in pixels at any zoom.
The floor ring is built from SDFs: a segmented band, four inward chevrons in the gaps and a counter-rotating tick ring.
Faction is one colour parameter. Elite adds a second ring, spikes and a double chevron rather than a new effect.
A slow sweep rides up the rim so the selection reads as alive without flashing.

name: Midas Touch
blurb: A touch on the shoulder spreads polished gold across the body behind a sparkling front line, then lets it go.
port: Material layer blend driven by a sphere mask from a touch position parameter plus noise. The gold layer needs a reflection capture or a cubemap parameter; sparkles spawn from the skeletal mesh surface with the same sphere mask as a kill test.
notes: The sweep is distance from the touch point plus noise and a crack channel, so gold runs ahead in thin fingers before the surface fills in.
Gold only reads as gold with something to reflect, so the metal samples a small procedural studio environment with a warm softbox and a horizon strip.
The front line is the sweep mask re-thresholded into a narrow emissive band, with hashed sparkle cells inside it.
Glints test random surface points against the front and only show inside the band. Dust uses the front position at its own birth time and falls away.
One tint is the metal reflectance and the glow colour, so silver, rose gold and jade come from the same effect.
